Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes is ‘plug-and-play’ midfielder transfer in Declan Rice mould who can help Arsenal win it all
Sports.content:
BRUNO GUIMARAES will help get Arsenal dancing to a different beat.

The Gunners relied on defensive steel to win the Prem last season but Mikel Arteta is aware of the need to evolve.



And what better way than by adding some Samba flair to the mix?

Midfield ace Guimaraes — set to join from Newcastle — certainly offers that.



And, who knows, there could be even more if Arsenal pull off a sensational swoop for his Brazil team-mate Vinicius Jr.

A mega-money deal for the Real Madrid winger looks very hard to do, yet Emirates chiefs at least hope to get Guimaraes through the door.



A deal for the Newcastle captain, 28, is at an advanced stage and he should arrive for a fee north of £70million.

That is a serious outlay but it makes sense after boss Arteta’s midfield struggles last season. Declan Rice and Martin Zubimendi were run into the ground and there is a clear need for reinforcements in that area.

Guimaraes brings something different to the party and will not be afraid to put his mark on this Arsenal team after becoming a leader at Newcastle.

The midfielder has developed the attacking part of his game since moving to Toon from Lyon in January 2022.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Last season was his most productive and the Brazilian finished it with nine league goals and five assists.

Viktor Gyokeres was the only Arsenal player who bettered that tally — with 14 Prem goals and a solitary assist.

The Gunners lacked an attacking threat from midfield on their way to winning the title but they struggled for creativity, too. Guimaraes showed with his four assists for Brazil at the World Cup this summer how he can help in this area.

That came off the back of a season where he created 45 Prem chances, with Rice and Bukayo Saka the only two Gunners to better that.



But no one in Arteta’s ranks could compete with Guimareas when it came to through balls and passes completed in the final third.

The latter has been a real problem for Arsenal, who especially struggle when teams sit deep.

Guimaraes is excellent at receiving the ball in tight spaces and can help pick the lock of stubborn defences.

His arrival can ease the creative burden on captain Martin Odegaard, who he might play alongside as a No 8.



Rice operating behind the pair would give the champions a solid base and the England star could easily dovetail with Guimaraes — adding attacking fluidity.

The Toon hero is set to join a handy Brazilian contingent at the Emirates — which includes Gabriel Jesus, Gabriel and Gabriel Martinelli. He would also be the latest in a long line of Samba stars to represent Arsenal, following in the footsteps of World Cup winner Gilberto Silva.

The midfielder was a bedrock of that Invincibles side in 2003-04, like fellow countryman Edu — who sparked Arsenal’s interest in Guimaraes.

Edu looked at bringing the midfielder to the Emirates six years ago when working as the club’s technical director.



Guimaraes was playing at Athletico Paranaense then and Arsenal continued to track him when he joined Lyon.

Finally, the playmaker looks on his way to North London — and his hunger to win trophies should prove infectious.

If Arteta was wary about anyone resting on their laurels after title glory, throwing in someone with Guimaraes’ fighting spirit will put paid to that.

And that is the attractive thing about the midfielder — who is able to combine Brazilian flair with English grit.



Per 90 minutes in the top flight last season, he won more duels and tackles than any Arsenal player. Arteta will love that because — as much as there is a need to liven up the Gunners’ attack — the Spaniard is never going to fully abandon his core principles.

Hard work is a huge part of that, and Guimaraes offers it in spades at a time when Arsenal want to kick on with their project.

Arteta is hungry for more success and conscious of the fact the club have never retained the Prem.

The Champions League remains an elusive prize, too, and the heartbreak of last season’s final shootout defeat to Paris Saint-Germain will serve as fuel.



Signing the experienced Guimaraes is an indication of how Arsenal want to win now, not simply build for the future.

The last time they spent this much on a midfielder was three years ago, when they paid West Ham £105m for Rice.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Arsenal chief Josh Kroenke called Rice a “plug-and-play” signing who could hit the ground running straight away.

If a deal gets over the line, Guimaraes will be expected to do the same.

Sports.title: Fifa SCRAPS Infantino’s £15billion plot to flog World Cup to private investors after football world erupts in anger
Sports.content:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino has scrapped plans to flog the World Cup to private investors amid global fury.

His bid to sell off a chunk of a new sister company in charge of the World Cup collapsed following Uefa’s boycott promise and a “brand nightmare” for potential investors.



On Tuesday it emerged that Infantino wanted to create a subsidiary called the Fifa Forward Enterprise, which would have presided over money-making assets including the World Cup.

Fifa valued the new branch at £15bn, and was hoping to sell a 20 per cent stake for £3.1bn.



But now the controversial plans have been scrapped following widespread opposition from football confederations, national associations and senior figures within the organisation.

In comments obtained by Sky News, Infantino said upon listening to “all the views” he recognised the “project has created divisions”.

He said: “The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.

“And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.

“Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place. Our purpose has always been – and will always be – to unite and improve.

“As a result, this proposal will not proceed. Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, particularly in those countries that mostly need our support.”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Thrive Capital, led by Joshua Kushner, Donald Trump‘s son-in-law Jared Kushner‘s brother, had been a front-runner to bid, with JPMorgan onboard in an advisory role.

But according to the New York Post, a source said of Kushner’s group: “They are not feeling this. There is no way they want to continue to be involved in this mess.

“Kushner will figure out another way to get involved in this space. This is becoming a brand nightmare.”

Uefa chief Aleksander Ceferin strongly opposed Fifa’s project from the start.



And on Thursday, Uefa’s 55 member associations, including England, agreed to boycott the World Cup should the Fifa Forward Enterprise come to fruition.

Fifa attempted to hang on to its plan, dangling £30million payments to its member associations should it be approved by September 19.

But Uefa’s boycott promise tanked the value of Fifa’s proposed deal – with Europe’s huge markets driving significant commercial interest from TV, sponsors and fans.

Concacaf and the AFC also publicly revealed their opposition to Infantino’s money-making vision, providing a further nail in its coffin.

Early on Friday Infantino was rocked by the resignation of one of his most senior advisers, Carlos Cordeiro.



The former US Soccer president told Sky News: “As a senior adviser to the Fifa president, a former banker, and a lifelong football fan, I cannot stand by while Fifa considers selling a stake in the World Cup.

“Let me be clear: I had no involvement in this proposal, and I oppose it unequivocally.

“It is a bad deal for Fifa’s Member Associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game.”

Fifa COO accuses Gianni Infantino of ‘deceiving’ governing body FIFA chief operating officer Kevin Lamour has blasted president Gianni Infantino’s shameless plot The COO is adamant this whole initiative was down to Infantino alone and he is personally so against it he is willing to step down. Lamour said: “To put it very clearly and directly: the project that has sparked so much controversy and debate is not a Fifa project. It is even less a project of Fifa’s administration. It is the project of one person. “The Fifa vice-presidents, the members of the Fifa Council, the confederations, the federations, the players, the leagues, the clubs, and the fans were not the only ones who were ignored. “Fifa’s own administration was also deceived. This lie by omission over many months and this unilateral exercise of power are not trivial. “They are indicative of a lack of trust, a lack of transparency, a lack of discernment, a lack of good governance. And a serious lack of respect. “Not only must this project not go ahead — for obvious reasons that need not even be listed here — but the time has now come for football political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions. “Regarding this project and what comes next. Everyone must take responsibility. Because it is becoming increasingly difficult for Fifa’s administration to work under these conditions and fulfil its mission. “My feeling is that we all want to be proud to work for Fifa, and today, unfortunately, it seems that is no longer the case for many of us. That saddens me. “My colleagues — some of whom have dedicated their lives to football — deserve better than contempt and intimidation. “The ball is now in the court of those who have the power to change things. I know I have a duty of loyalty to my employer. “But I also, and above all, have a duty of loyalty to certain values and to the upbringing I have received, and a duty to support my colleagues. “And if that means I lose my job, then so be it. I will understand and respect that decision. At least I’ll sleep well tonight.”

As the project crumbled around them, Fifa still attempted to plough on.

A shameless statement on Friday read: “We have heard the feedback provided by the respective confederations in relation to the proposed establishment of Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) and would like to address the issues that have surfaced since the initial media reporting on Tuesday.



“We respect the feedback and concern aired in public and reaffirm our commitment to an open and democratic consultation.

“Our planned consultation process was disrupted by incorrect media reports.

“We will proceed with this consultation process to ensure that each MA has the ability to express its vote based on facts.

“FFE has been proposed solely to ensure that all Fifa Member Associations (MAs) have the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of the commercial opportunity of football in their respective countries, and that this does not come at the cost of either the spirit or the governance of FIFA or football itself.

“Nobody is selling football. This is not something Fifa would ever entertain.



“Everyone has the right to express their opposition and to seek further clarification but no single entity can claim to represent all 211 MAs around the world.

“Each MA should be allowed to review the proposal and have a say in shaping their own future. These are the democratic principles of Fifa.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Infantino, dubbed “the most hated man in football“, now finds himself under huge pressure.

Sports.title: Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha ‘set for stunning transfer U-turn’ despite already being ANNOUNCED by new club
Sports.content:
CAPE VERDE star Vozinha is set for a massive transfer U-turn by snubbing a famous club that already announced his arrival.

The 40-year-old goalkeeper made headlines this summer by leading his underdog country to an historic campaign that saw them picking up famous draws against world champions Spain, Uruguay and Saudi Arabia.



The keeper’s incredible saves led Cape Verde to the play-offs of their first World Cup appearance and came close to stunning Argentina at extra-time before falling heroically in a 3-2 defeat.

Vozinha’s stunning displays between the sticks earned him a place in the World Cup’s team of the tournament alongside superstars like Lionel Messi, Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappe.



And that led to a call-up from Chilean giants Colo-Colo who have been close to signing him as a free agent following his departure from Chaves in June.

According to journalist Raphael Bozeo, however, Moroccan outfit Berkane are set to hijack the deal.



That is despite the fact Colo-Colo already announced Vozinha‘s arrival at the Monumental last week.

However, the Cape Verde international postponed his arrival in Santiago three different times and thus caused uncertainty about his move.

Vozinha was initially expected to arrive in Chile on Tuesday before the flight was rescheduled for Wednesday.

But plans changed again and the shot-stopper was expected on Thursday but nothing came of it.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

And Berkane are now expected to swoop in amid reports suggesting they have also agreed with Vozinha’s Cape Verde manager Bubista to take over as their new head coach.

The same source now claims Vozinha is expecting an official offer from the Moroccans.

This comes after it was revealed the goalie won’t be allowed to don his famous nickname on the back of his shirt with Colo-Colo as per Chilean football rules.

Vozinha, whose birth name is Josimar Jose Evora Dias, will instead have to choose between ‘Evora’, ‘Dias’ or ‘Evora Dias’.

Sports.title: Footie club launch new kit with a THOUSAND sponsors in bid to head off financial crisis
Sports.content:
FOUR-TIME national champions Deportivo Municipal are trying to avoid bankruptcy in truly unique style.

The fallen Peruvian giants have unveiled a new kit plastered with a mind-blowing 1,000 sponsors, raising over £220,000 in the process.



An impending threat of financial liquidation forced the Lima-based outfit to think outside the box, and the top brass responded by turning their shirt into an advertising hoarding.

The hyper-commercial kit marks a new, visually striking chapter in the club’s current off-field firestorm.



As recently as 2017, Deportivo Municipal were going toe-to-toe with South America’s finest in the Copa Libertadores, and the side were still in the domestic top flight just three years ago.

But the debt-saddled club were subsequently dealt a slew of points deductions which saw them relegated to the second division for the 2023/24 season.

Barely a year later, ‘Muni’ were banished to Liga 3 after being unable to fork up the funds for their license to the Peruvian Football Federation.

Earlier this year, their situation reached a new level of desolation when they were disqualified from the professional pyramid and consigned to the Copa Perú.

Before this snazzy new design, Deportivo sported a minimalist shirt, featuring a classy white base emblazoned with a red sash.

While Austrian Bundesliga side Hartberg once made headlines for having 23 sponsors splashed across their kit – including a sperm-boosting brand.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The iconic Peruvian club have now blown that figure out the water.

The astonishing shirt is a unique and desperate fundraising attempt, after dire finances forced the club to carve their kit into 1,000 advertising squares and launch the ‘Los Mil Sponsors del Muni’ (The Thousand Sponsors of Muni’) campaign in January.

Local businesses were quick to snap up the miniature slots, listed for 200 Peruvian soles apiece (roughly £44), selling out the commercial venture within three months.

Muni’s plethora of new backers includes nearby wineries and pet shops, all keen to pump life into the sinking club.



Despite the short-term cash injection and international media storm their kit has whipped up, Deportivo Municipal were knocked out of the Copa Perú last weekend in a bitter blow to their attempted renaissance.

Sports.title: Next Fifa tournament set to go AHEAD despite England and Uefa announcing boycott as statement released
Sports.content:
POLISH football chiefs expect to stage the U-20 Women’s World Cup as planned in September… despite Uefa’s boycott of Fifa competitions.

Fifa president Gianni Infantino plunged world football into chaos earlier this week with his hated plan to privatise the World Cup.



Infantino wants to launch and sell stakes in a subsidiary, named the Fifa Forward Enterprise, to oversee Fifa competitions, including the World Cup.

The greedy plan sparked outcry across football, with Uefa member associations agreeing to BOYCOTT Fifa tournaments during an emergency meeting on Thursday.



Despite this stance, the Polish FA (PZPN) expect to go ahead with the U-20 Women’s World Cup between September 5-27 as planned.

Their general secretary Lukasz Wachowski told The Athletic: “As the host association, we are fully prepared to deliver the tournament and continue to implement all necessary preparations in line with the agreed schedule.

“We remain in close contact with our partners at Uefa and are working in accordance with our joint arrangements.

“We believe that the current situation will be resolved swiftly, allowing young players from across the world to compete in Poland in a tournament that, for many of them, will represent the fulfilment of a dream and an important milestone in their sporting careers.”

England are scheduled to take part in the competition and have been drawn in Group B alongside Brazil, Canada and Tanzania.

But FA chiefs are committed to Uefa’s boycott plan.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

In addition to the U-20 Women’s World Cup, there is also scheduled to be an Under-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco and Under-17 Men’s World Cup in Qatar before the end of the year.

Fifa need a majority of its 211 members to vote through its hated privatisation plan before September 19 to proceed.

The project was left in tatters as Uefa announced its boycott – with Concacaf and the AFC also criticising plans.

Fifa have shamelessly vowed to plough on, for now, saying in a statement: “We have heard the feedback provided by the respective confederations in relation to the proposed establishment of Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) and would like to address the issues that have surfaced since the initial media reporting on Tuesday.



“We respect the feedback and concern aired in public and reaffirm our commitment to an open and democratic consultation.

“Our planned consultation process was disrupted by incorrect media reports.

“We will proceed with this consultation process to ensure that each MA has the ability to express its vote based on facts.

“FFE has been proposed solely to ensure that all Fifa Member Associations (MAs) have the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of the commercial opportunity of football in their respective countries, and that this does not come at the cost of either the spirit or the governance of FIFA or football itself.

“Nobody is selling football. This is not something Fifa would ever entertain.



“Everyone has the right to express their opposition and to seek further clarification but no single entity can claim to represent all 211 MAs around the world.

“Each MA should be allowed to review the proposal and have a say in shaping their own future. These are the democratic principles of Fifa.”

The plan is to sell 20 per cent of the World Cup to private investors for £3.2billion – which values the new commercial arm at £15billion.

The scheme would include a payment of £30m to all 211 countries “irrespective” of their support for the plans.

American firm Thrive Capital, whose CEO is Donald Trump‘s son-in-law Jared Kushner‘s brother Joshua, are thought be front-runners to invest, should the project go ahead.

Sports.content:
Chelsea and FA drop Mykhailo Mudryk statement

Mykhailo Mudryk will now be available to play for Chelsea. A statement from the FA confirmed the news, saying: "The FA can confirm that the anti-doping disciplinary proceedings against Mykhailo Mudryk were resolved with the agreement of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) on 30 July 2026.

"In the context of that agreement, Mr Mudryk has accepted his commission of Anti-Doping Rule Violations (ADRVs) and accepted a period of ineligibility. On 22 October 2024, Mr Mudryk was subject to an out-of-competition doping control, which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance.

"The FA notified Mr Mudryk of that finding on 4 December 2024 and imposed a provisional suspension. On 23 May 2025, The FA charged Mr Mudryk with ADRVs in breach of Regulations 3 and 4 of its 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations.

"On 7 to 9 January 2026, a hearing took place before an independent Regulatory Commission. The Regulatory Commission found that Mr Mudryk had committed the charged ADRVs and imposed a four-year period of ineligibility. Subsequently, Mr Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

"Since then, changes have been made to WADA Technical Document (TD2027MRL) which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk's sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no ADRVs would have resulted.

"Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, The FA and Mr Mudryk have now - with the agreement of WADA - resolved the appeal proceedings in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the World Anti-Doping Code and Regulation 90 of the 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations.

"As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the Anti-Doping Rule Violations charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement. Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect."

Chelsea also uploaded their own statement which said: "Chelsea FC acknowledges today's announcement by The Football Association confirming the resolution of the anti-doping proceedings involving Mykhailo Mudryk.

"From the outset, this has been an extremely difficult period for Misha, both professionally and personally, and we are pleased that the matter has now reached a conclusion which allows him to return to football with immediate effect.

"We have always supported Misha throughout this process while fully respecting the integrity of the anti-doping system and the legal process. We welcome the acknowledgement that advances in the applicable scientific reporting standards for more reliable testing mean that, had Misha's sample been analysed under today's technical requirements, it would not have been reported as a positive test and no anti-doping rule violation would have resulted.

"That is an important part of the context surrounding the agreed resolution and allows everyone involved to move forward. "Misha has consistently maintained that he never knowingly or intentionally used a prohibited substance and did not know how traces of the substance entered his system. Throughout this process he has conducted himself professionally and with resilience during what has undoubtedly been one of the most challenging periods of his career.

"We know how much this opportunity to return means to him. Our focus now is on supporting Misha’s reintegration into the squad and helping him resume his career. Chelsea FC remains fully committed to the highest standards of sporting integrity and compliance with all anti-doping regulations. Everyone at the Club now looks forward to helping Misha return to full fitness, back into the squad and back onto the pitch."

Sports.title: Eddie Howe fell out with two players before Newcastle United exit – 'promises are broken'
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe fell out with two players before Newcastle United exit – 'promises are broken'

Eddie Howe's tenure as Newcastle United manager is over after almost five years at the helm

View 3 Images Eddie Howe didn't see eye to eye with every Newcastle player (Image: Newcastle United via Getty Image)

Eddie Howe has been adored by the majority of players he has worked with. The now ex-Newcastle United manager can reflect on a strong relationship with a host of stars during his time on Tyneside.

‌



But when you've managed a club for almost five years, it's impossible to stay on good terms with everyone. And there have been a couple of instances where relations have turned sour.

‌



The most obvious example is Alexander Isak, who pushed for a transfer to Liverpool last summer. As speculation cranked up, the Swedish striker was left out of a pre-season game at Celtic and a tour of Asia, as he was made to train on his own.

‌



To his credit, Howe refrained from criticising Isak, even though he was clearly unhappy about the situation. The same could not be said of the player himself, who issued an explosive social media statement in which he slammed the Magpies and claimed promises had been broken.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"The reality is that promises were made and the club has known my position for a long time. To now act as if these issues are only emerging is misleading," he wrote.

‌



Bruno Guimaraes shares emotional Eddie Howe message after Newcastle exit READ MORE :

Newcastle United confirm Eddie Howe exit with statement issued as replacement lined up READ MORE :

"When promises are broken and trust is lost, the relationship can't continue. That's where things are for me right now - and why change is in the best interests of everyone, not just myself."

Of course, Isak eventually got his way as he joined Liverpool for a British transfer record £125million. The saga was arguably the beginning of the end of Howe's tenure.

View 3 Images Howe's relationship with Alexander Isak became strained (Image: Getty)

‌



Going back further, Howe also had a frosty relationship with Ryan Fraser. The pair actually fell out at Bournemouth amid a disagreement over a short-term extension when the Cherries needed him to sign a deal to help them stay up in 2020.

Fraser went on to join Newcastle, then managed by Steve Bruce, but the pair were reunited in 2021. By 2023, Fraser was training with the under-21s, with Howe openly admitting the Scot had no future at the club.

Howe said: "I'd never put a firm decision on that [whether Fraser has a future at the club] because life and football can change quickly. But I'd say, at the moment, no he doesn't.

‌



View 3 Images Ryan Fraser was frozen out at Newcastle by Howe (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

"Ryan's training with the under-21s. I made the decision to concentrate on players that are committed to Newcastle. For the benefit of the group, I've made that call."

Earlier this year, Fraser insisted he had no hard feelings towards Howe, calling him a 'father figure' during his time at Bournemouth and saying: "He can make any player in this world better."

Sports.title: Ryan Reynolds showed true colours in private message to Man Utd star after pre-season blow
Sports.content:
Ryan Reynolds showed true colours in private message to Man Utd star after pre-season blow

Things got a little testy when Manchester United faced Wrexham in pre-season back in 2023, at which point Ryan Reynolds showed his true colours

View 2 Images Ryan Reynolds showed his true colours (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images)

Ryan Reynolds showed a classy side after reaching out to a Manchester United goalkeeper following Wrexham's pre-season meeting with the Red Devils in 2023. The friendly, which Wrexham won 3-1, was overshadowed by a serious injury to striker Paul Mullin, who suffered a punctured lung after colliding with United goalkeeper Nathan Bishop.

‌



Bishop had raced off his line in an attempt to clear the ball as Mullin broke through on goal, catching the Wrexham forward with a heavy challenge. Mullin was treated with oxygen on the pitch before being taken to hospital, while the visibly upset Bishop later contacted him to apologise.

‌



Although Reynolds was not at the match, he learned of both the incident and Bishop's gesture afterwards. It later emerged that the Wrexham co-owner personally messaged the United goalkeeper to praise the way he had handled the situation and wished him well for the future.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Not Man Utd or Liverpool – this is who fans are backing most to win the Premier League READ MORE :

A few days later, Reynolds made light of the incident, joking that fellow Wrexham co-owner Rob McElhenney would be "having a word" with Bishop. Speaking to former UK Prime Minister Rishi Sunak on the set of Deadpool 3, Reynolds said: "The UK is my favourite place to make a movie. I'm hoping to see even more film work head to Wales.

"Rob would have joined but he's currently having a word with Man United's youth team goalie."

‌



While Reynolds was able to see the funny side, Wrexham manager Phil Parkinson was far less forgiving. He described Bishop's challenge as "reckless" and "clumsy", and even suggested the goalkeeper should "steer clear" of Wrexham in future.

His anger was understandable given Mullin's importance to the club. Between the 2021/22 and 2023/24 seasons, the striker scored 105 goals in 140 appearances, cementing his place among Wrexham's greatest goalscorers and playing a pivotal role in the club's rapid rise through the Football League.

View 2 Images Paul Mullin (L) was hospitalised after colliding with Nathan Bishop (R) during a pre-season friendly between Wrexham and Man Utd in 2023 (Image: 2023 Getty Images)

‌



However, Mullin found goals much harder to come by after Wrexham's promotion to League One, scoring just five times in 32 appearances across all competitions during the 2024/25 campaign. Following the club's promotion to the Championship in 2025, he was loaned to Wigan Athletic before spending the second half of last season at Bradford City, where he failed to score in nine appearances.

Bishop, meanwhile, never made a senior appearance for Manchester United before leaving the club shortly after the incident to join then-Championship side Sunderland.

The move failed to kick-start his career, however. After making just two appearances for the Black Cats, he was sent out on loan to Wycombe Wanderers and Cambridge United before joining AFC Wimbledon last season. The move finally gave the 26-year-old a sustained run of first-team football - his first since a loan spell at Mansfield Town during the 2021/22 campaign.

Article continues below

Wrexham came close to setting up more meetings with Manchester United last season after narrowly missing out on a Championship play-off place. They finished seventh, two points behind Hull City, who went on to secure promotion to the Premier League by beating Millwall and Middlesbrough in the play-offs.

Sports.title: Football legend's son retired aged 29 due to 'boredom' and now denied World Cup spot
Sports.content:
Football legend's son retired aged 29 due to 'boredom' and now denied World Cup spot

The football icon's son has blew his chance of featuring in the World Cup

View 3 Images Enzo Zidane retired from the sport at 29 (Image: Getty)

The son of the legendary Zinedine Zidane, Enzo, retired from football at just 29 due to boredom. The premature ending of his career means he has missed out on a potential call-up to the French national team, with Zidane Sr the new boss of Les Bleus.

‌



Zidane, the Real Madrid icon, has taken over the position from Didier Deschamps, who stepped down after guiding France to the last four of the World Cup this summer. However, Enzo, now 31, will not be a part of his dad's squad after curtailing his professional career.

‌



Enzo was eligible to play for France, Spain, and through his paternal grandparents, Algeria. The midfielder made one appearance for Spain under-15s but switched allegiances to France in 2014.

‌



Enzo began his career with Italian giants Juventus in 2000, for whom his father also played. He signed for another of his father's teams, Real, in 2004. Following stints in the Spanish capital's C and B squads, his maiden appearance for the first team arrived in 2016. Managed by his father at the time, he even managed to find the back of the net during his senior debut.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Italy in turmoil as legend ready to quit 16 days into job after manager pick blocked READ MORE :

England to play two of seven Euro 2028 matches away from Wembley in best-case scenario READ MORE :

His early promise fizzled out, however, and he was unable to establish himself as a regular at the Santiago Bernabeu. He subsequently bounced around various teams in Spain, Switzerland, Portugal and France.

‌



Departing Madrid, Enzo signed for La Liga side Alaves, though he featured only twice for them. He then moved to Lausanne-Sport in Switzerland, a spell that concluded with him being loaned back to Spanish club Rayo Majadahonda.

His time in Portugal with Aves was short-lived, yielding just 11 games, before he finished his playing days with Almeria, French team Rodez, and, finally, Spanish fourth-tier outfit Fuenlabrada.

View 3 Images Zinedine ZIdane and Enzo Zidane were together at Real Madrid (Image: Helios de la Rubia/Real Madrid via Getty Images)

‌



His eventual loss of passion for the sport is largely understandable, given that he had not played a competitive match since May 2023, leaving him without a team for a staggering 16 months. According to the Spanish outlet AS, Enzo had simply lost interest, though he had previously admitted that carrying the heavy burden of being Zinedine's son was immensely taxing.

The AS report noted that Enzo is currently dedicating his time to his spouse and three children. He has been open about the difficulties of living up to the massive legacy left by his dad, however.

Enzo explained to Marca: "It has been there since my childhood [being compared to his dad], and it will perpetually remain that way. That isn't shifting, yet I strive to distance myself from the noise and concentrate on becoming the greatest Enzo I can be.

‌



"The public measures you against him, judges you, demands extra from you, and claims your success is just because of your parentage. People face judgment for all sorts of reasons, but I attempt to block it out. What truly matters is making my family proud. I simply focus on evolving as Enzo, nothing more."

View 3 Images Zidane won three Champions Leagues and two La Liga titles as Real Madrid manager (Image: Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Zidane has three other sons, all of whom are professional footballers. Theo, 24, is a midfielder for Cordoba, Luca, 28, plays in goal for Granada, and 20-year-old Elyaz currently lines up for Red Star in France.

‌



Zidane Snr. is widely regarded as one of the greatest players in history. The 1998 World Cup champion won two Serie A titles while at Juventus. Following an unprecedented £46million transfer to Real Madrid in 2001, he went on to lift both the La Liga trophy and the Champions League.

The 1998 Ballon d'Or recipient enjoyed an even more illustrious period while managing the Spanish heavyweights. Over the course of two separate managerial tenures, he secured a duo of La Liga championships alongside a trio of Champions League titles.

He was confirmed as the new manager of the France national team on Tuesday, saying in a statement: "I have often said, ‘There is nothing greater than the French national team’.

Article continues below

"It is therefore a joy – and obviously a source of great pride – to become the head coach of this French team. It is also a responsibility. Needless to say, I have great ambitions for the French national team!"

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta has 'saved Arsenal £35million' with one shrewd piece of transfer business
Sports.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Mikel Arteta has 'saved Arsenal £35million' with one shrewd piece of transfer business

Mikel Arteta and his recruitment team may have already snagged a transfer deal this summer that could end up saving Arsenal tens of millions

View 2 Images New Arsenal purchase Christos Tzolis has been backed to prove himself as a bargain signing (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

New Arsenal signing Christos Tzolis has been backed to save the Gunners a fortune in the transfer market. Mikel Arteta's men plundered Belgium's Pro League to sign its best performer of the last two seasons, who could have gone for a lot more.

‌



At least that's the assertion made by Belgian football expert Scott Coyne, who feels the £34.1million man may have gone for twice as much if he were playing in one of Europe's more prominent divisions. As it is, however, Arteta & Co are hoping they've got their hands on a steal after identifying Leandro Trossard's replacement.

‌



Tzolis, 24, enjoyed a hugely prolific two-season spell in Bruges, where he contributed 43 goals and 45 assists in 108 appearances. And The Belgian Football Podcast's Coyne has tipped the former Norwich prospect to prove his value in the long run.

‌



"I think Arsenal have got a good deal here. It’s the biggest outgoing transfer in Belgian football history, just pipping a couple of others that are just under that, just taking over from Charles de Ketelaere’s move when he went to AC Milan," he told Mirror Football.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"They could easily have paid more. I think the thing with Belgian football is the top clubs, even the top clubs, get mugged a little bit because of their place in the food chain. If Tzolis had been producing these numbers in Germany or France or something, then Arsenal would probably be paying upwards of £60m or £70m for him."

‌



Arsenal have been left without a choice as Mikel Arteta's transfer frustrations clear READ MORE :

It stands to reason that a player with 51 goal contributions (22 goals and 29 assists) in only 52 games last term would command such a fee. And it's a mark of the upgrades Tzolis has made to his game since a middling three-year stretch on the books at Norwich.

Fair to say the winger has improved tremendously since then. Just as Viktor Gyokeres is no longer the player who failed to break through at Brighton years prior to joining Arsenal, Tzolis is new and improved compared to his time with the Canaries.

"So it’s not a bad deal," said Coyne, who also runs a football consultancy company. "But I think it’s just one of these things that people haven’t remarked on with this deal, that the club could have gotten more. They won’t be unhappy with that.

‌



View 2 Images Tzolis' £34million fee makes him the most expensive signing from Belgium's Pro League (Image: Getty )

"They regularly do deals for pretty much around the, yes, certainly over the £30m mark, which is extraordinary to do that on a regular basis for a club of that size. So, yes, I think Arsenal are getting him cheaply."

The £34.1m fee looks like terrific business in a market where nine-digit signings have become increasingly common. Arsenal also managed to squeeze up to £17m out of Trossard's move to Besiktas, meaning half of Tzolis' cost is effectively accounted for before he's kicked a ball.

‌



He's currently on course to compete with Gabriel Martinelli for that left-sided slot in Arteta's attack. However, the player's malleability and ability to play off either foot - though he's naturally right-footed - makes him a versatile asset providing options in numerous positions.

Sports.title: Tottenham’s dream final month of transfer window as two top signings sealed and three exits
Sports.content:
Tottenham’s dream final month of transfer window as two top signings sealed and three exits

Tottenham have already made a number of signings this summer and are keen to secure more

View 4 Images Tottenham Hotspur manager Roberto De Zerbi (Image: Alex Pantling/Getty Images)

Tottenham are planning to further strengthen their squad despite having already spent £237million this summer. Spurs have secured Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Jan Paul van Hecke so far to bolster their midfield and backline.

‌



Andy Robertson, Marcos Senesi and Martin Dubravka have also moved to north London, saving Roberto De Zerbi funds as they all arrive on free transfers. Despite five players already coming through the doors of the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the manager is not planning on slowing his transfer plans down anytime soon.

‌



Discussing his process after the 2-0 friendly win against Auckland on Sunday, De Zerbi said: "It is not finished yet, our transfer market. I think we can be happier at the end of this transfer market, because I spoke a lot to the owner, the board, and they want to build a very strong team for this season, but to make the base for the future to become great again."

‌



A number of Premier League stars have been linked with the Lilywhites, including Savinho, Marcus Rashford and Eli Junior Kroupi. Here, Mirror Football has outlined how Spurs can achieve the ideal start to their 2026/27 season as the transfer window enters its final month.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Wantaway Tottenham star emerges on Arsenal and Chelsea radar in transfer twist READ MORE :

Rashford signs

Spurs have made little secret of their pursuit of Rashford - yet Manchester United are unwilling to sell him to a rival Premier League club. The iPaper reports that United are firmly against facing their academy product in the top flight, with club insiders reportedly fearing "humiliation" should he score against his former employers.

However, the club's top brass have been outspoken about their desire to remove his whopping £350,000-a-week wages from their books. This could hand Tottenham the opening to make a rapid move for the England international.

View 4 Images Marcus Rashford could head to north London (Image: Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



Rashford enjoyed a stellar spell with Barcelona last season, racking up 28 goal contributions and playing his part in their La Liga title triumph. De Zerbi would need to seal a deal ahead of Arsenal and Chelsea, both of whom have been closely monitoring the 28-year-old.

De Zerbi wish granted

The Tottenham manager has made no secret of his desire to bring more attacking-minded players into his ranks. Several names have been touted, among them Bournemouth's Eli Junior Kroupi and Franco Mastantuono of Real Madrid.

Kroupi would represent a shrewd acquisition - but the Bournemouth forward has attracted attention from numerous leading clubs across Europe and may ultimately prove too costly. Meanwhile, Real are reportedly only willing to let Mastantuono depart on a temporary basis this summer.

‌



View 4 Images Savinho is a key target for De Zerbi (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

However, Manchester City's Savinho appears to be the ideal wide player for Spurs to pursue. The winger is receptive to a departure, according to BBC Sport, with a switch to Tottenham emerging as a realistic possibility.

The 22-year-old represents a priority target for De Zerbi, with Tottenham conducting discussions last summer about securing his move to north London. City showed no interest in selling at that point but may now be willing to allow Savinho to leave as he seeks more playing opportunities.

‌



Outcast stars depart

Spurs will equally be eager to offload some of their fringe players, whether on loan or permanently. The Daily Mail reports West Ham are interested in acquiring Manor Solomon from Tottenham, with the winger seeking an exit.

View 4 Images Cristian Romero is keen on a summer exit (Image: George Wood/Getty Images)

Solomon has featured in merely six matches for the club over three seasons, spending time at Villarreal, Fiorentina and Leeds. The player's representative has made it clear that a loan arrangement is not desired, with the Hammers likely having to pay approximately £7m for his signature.

‌



Club captain Cristian Romero has been linked with numerous clubs and is anticipated to depart this summer. Tottenham are reportedly demanding £42.8m for his services, with Inter Milan, Chelsea, Barcelona and Atletico Madrid among the sides to have been mentioned as potential suitors.

Portuguese publication Maisfutebol reports that Porto are pursuing Spurs defender Souza. The left-back was originally recruited during the January transfer window as backup for Djed Spence.

However, the left-back managed just four Premier League outings and could be heading for the exit door after only six months in the capital. With Destiny Udogie and Andrew Robertson likely to rank above him in the pecking order, a departure could suit all concerned - even if it is only on a temporary basis.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Green light given for huge transfer offer as talks for new signing begin
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Green light given for huge transfer offer as talks for new signing begin

Liverpool continue to be connected with a number of potential transfers as we enter August

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola is looking to add to his squad this summer (Image: ISI Photos via Getty Images)

It's not been the hectic summer of transfer activity that many Liverpool fans would've hoped for so far. That said, the club could be edging closer to landing Bradley Barcola from PSG with the Reds and the European champions reportedly in talks over the winger.

‌



Neither of the club's new signings, Jeremy Jacquet or Victor Munoz, have featured for Andoni Iraola in pre-season yet due to injury and an extended break after the World Cup, respectively.

‌



Liverpool have looked sharp in wins over Sunderland and Wrexham, but new blood is needed. Today's news sees one potential target emerge after the player's club invited offers, while the Reds have been linked with a shock move for a former Premier League defender, with talks said to be underway.

‌



Liverpool given green light to make huge offer

Japanese international Kaishu Sano has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer. The sporting director of his club Mainz, Christian Heidel, has admitted the Bundesliga side could let the midfielder leave, but only for a huge fee.

The 25-year-old scored for Japan at this summer’s World Cup against Brazil. He has reportedly attracted interest from Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Liverpool's significant Bradley Barcola transfer boost as PSG close in on replacement READ MORE :

In an interview with BILD, Heidel opened up on the Mainz star's future, admitting that they'd have to accept a huge offer from a big club if one arrived. "You know we like to prepare transfers in such a way that the public only finds out once we announce them," he said.

"I won't comment on any rumours or discuss any of the clubs mentioned. We don't have to sell Kaishu; we can afford to keep him. If he stays, there will be a lot of happy people in the squad, the club, and the surrounding community.

"But it’s the same as always at Mainz 05: if an offer comes along that makes us gasp for breath, we have to consider it! There’s no doubt there are interested parties,” he told BILD, as quoted by Sport Witness. “It’s well known that England is the league where outstanding players usually move.

‌



View 3 Images Kaishu Sano celebrates scoring against Brazil. (Image: Lars Baron/Getty Images)

“Our big advantage is that the player still has a long-term contract, so we’re under no pressure at all and won’t be rushing anything. If a club comes along with an offer, we’ll consider it. If, in our view, it’s not high enough for the player’s market value, then it’s also possible that Kaishu will stay with us longer.

“As of today, everything is still open. But we know, of course, that we have a player who is generating a lot of interest.”

‌



'Talks underway' for ex-Premier League star

Italian outlet Tutto Juve claims that Liverpool have held initial discussions with AC Milan over a move for Fikayo Tomori, who previously played for Chelsea.

The report says that "discussions are currently still in the early stages and negotiations are not yet advanced" as Liverpool evaluate how much a move for the former Chelsea defender would cost.

Tomori has a deal with Milan until 2027, meaning the Serie A side don't need to sell but do risk losing him for free next year. The centre-back came up through the youth system at Stamford Bridge before joining Milan five years ago.

‌



View 3 Images Tomori won the league with Milan in 2022 (Image: AC Milan via Getty Images)

The 28-year-old former England international's move to the San Siro has been a success. Tomori has played 214 times for the club, winning Serie A in 2022 and the Supercoppa Italiana in 2025.

Iraola's need for a new centre-back was exacerbated this week with the news that Joe Gomez would miss the start of the season through injury. New signing Jacquet is also yet to play for the Reds due to a minor injury.

Article continues below

Defenders Ibrahima Konate and Andrew Robertson have also left the club this summer, while young Italian centre-back Giovanni Leoni and right-back Conor Bradley are yet to return to training after their own injuries.

Sports.title: Haaderr and Suspicious Mindz clash at Doncaster
Sports.content:
We have a busy day's racing on Saturday with flat action from Doncaster and Lingfield Park live on Sky Sports Racing...

4.15 Doncaster - Haaderr and Suspicious Mindz top strong field

A strong edition of the Winners Wear Skopes Menswear Handicap sees Haaderr and Suspicious Mindz spearhead a field of five.

The Ed Bethell-trained Haaderr built on a pair of promising efforts to break his maiden at Southwell in October and, having undergone a gelding operation, he returned to a disappointing fourth of four at Catterick. That was his handicap introduction, and he could be capable of better.

Suspicious Mindz scored at the eighth attempt when landing a Curragh maiden on his final start for Jessica Harrington and he looks an interesting contender on his handicap bow for Seb Spencer.

Plenty have chances including First Time, while Vidmiyr has Jude Fernandes claiming a handy 7lbs.

5.05 Lingfield - Bintknight, Epictetus and Percival headline

Bintknight and Percival headline a field of five for this Professional Horse Racing Tips At chracingclub.com Handicap at Lingfield.

Harry Charlton's Bintknight is one of two three-year-olds in here and showed a good attitude when winning over this track and trip back in May. He made a pleasing handicap debut when runner-up at Doncaster and could go well off this one-pound higher mark.

Fellow three-year-old Starlight Time has been a tad disappointing in better company and should appreciate these calmer waters.

Percival and Epictetus must be considered. The former was a bit keen when third at Sandown and might have more to offer after just six starts, while Epictetus went down by just a neck at Epsom on his last outing.

10.52 Colonial Downs - Grade One Arlington Million Stakes - Burnham Square and Test Score clash

A brilliant field has assembled for this Grade One Arlington Million Stakes at Colonial Downs with Burnham Square sure to be popular for Ian Wilkes.

Winner of his last three outings, he justified short odds when landing the Chorleywood Stakes at Churchill Downs and will need to be at his best if he is to claim a second top-level success.

Test Score rates a big danger for Graham Motion. A dual Grade One victor, he returned to form with an excellent second in the Manhattan Stakes and a similar effort would see him hit the frame.

Of the others, Integration, Dresden Row and Gran Oriente make most appeal.

Best of the rest

4.00 Clairefontaine - Simon and Ed Crisford saddle Treble Tee in a Listed heat. Phineas is a useful type for the Wertheimers.

4.35 Clairefontaine - Listed contest where Alla Stella represents Sir Mark Prescott.

2.30am Del Mar - Grade One Clement L Hirsch Stakes - Chasten and Seismic Beauty will be popular.

10.44 Saratoga - Grade Two Jim Dandy - Renegade and Commandment headline a hot contest.

6.15 Lingfield - Tom Collins' Horse-To-Follow Campeona bids for a hat-trick.

2.30 Doncaster - A fair nursery with Encounter and Weleyff among five runners.

George Scott - 50% at Doncaster this season.

Sports.title: Leeds thrash Toulouse as Wigan beat Leigh
Sports.content:
Jake Connor starred as Super League leaders Leeds ran in eight tries in a 46-0 rout of Toulouse while Wigan Warriors remain just two points behind after their 20-8 win over Leigh Leopards.

Connor scored two of those tries himself and converted seven as the Rhinos ran up the score. Ned McCormack had an early try disallowed for a knock-on but it was merely a temporary stay of execution for Toulouse on a long night for the visitors.

Twelve minutes in Connor found a gap with the help of Riley Lumb to get the first, and it was then Connor who set up Mikolaj Oledzki for the second try of the night with a no-look pass. On the stroke of half-time Tom Holroyd added a third thanks to an offload from Presley Cassell.

The onslaught continued in the second half. James McDonnell found a gap four minutes after the restart, and just before the hour Leeds shifted the ball from wing to wing for Harry Newman to cross in the corner - although for the first time on the night Connor missed the conversion.

He made amends four minutes later by scoring his second try of the night, hauling in a catch before touching down. And Leeds kept on the pressure with late tries from Brodie Croft and Lumb padding an already lop-sided score-line.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Leeds Rhinos against Toulouse Olympique from the Super League

Wigan keep in touch with key victory

Wigan made it 10 consecutive wins in all competitions as they beat neighbours Leigh Leopards 20-8.

It was a typically full-throttle encounter from the start, with the first points scored from the boot of Leigh's Adam Cook after nine minutes following an infringement in front of the posts on Umyla Hanley.

The lead was extended to 6-0 five minutes later when the Leopards ended a period of pressure by working the ball out to Innes Senior on the left and he went over in the corner.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Innes Senior dives into the corner which gave Leigh Leopards an early lead over Wigan Warriors

The Leopards threw bodies on the line to keep out Wigan as they tried to take advantage of a couple of errors from the hosts, and the visitors thought they had reduced the deficit with 29 minutes gone.

Jake Wardle broke from his own line and found Liam Marshall, who sprinted almost the length of the field to touch down in the corner, but Wardle was penalised for a push on Hanley following a video review. Cook chose to go for goal from the penalty and extended the lead to eight points.

Leigh's defence had been exceptional but three minutes before the break they switched off as Field sprinted away following a penalty deep in his own half, breaking clean through the Leopards line and reaching the posts before anyone could catch him.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Matt Peet reacts to his side's victory over Leigh Leopard which extends Wigan Warriors unbeaten to eight games in the league

Harry Smith's kick reduced the arrears further, and four minutes after the break the visitors took the lead. Jack Hughes tried an extra pass, Noah Hodkinson picked up the loose ball and found Bevan French, who ran in under the posts.

Leigh coach Adrian Lam's expression darkened further in the 51st minute when his side were again made to pay dearly for a handling mistake, this time in-form Zach Eckersley intercepting and running away to the line.

And it was soon to get even worse, with smart handling from the Warriors after another Leopards error seeing Eckersley brilliantly play in Hodkinson for a fourth try in the corner.

Leigh tried to find a way back into the contest but Wigan stood firm to open up a six-point lead over their rivals and hand the Leopards a first defeat in six.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Hull KR against Bradford Bulls from the Super League

The other match on Friday saw Joe Burgess reach a career milestone of 200 tries after he scored twice in Hull KR's 40-16 win against Bradford Bulls.

Hull KR led 16-10 at half time before Jez Litten, Tom Davies and Elliot Minchella all scored in the second half to send the reigning champions into the top four.

Sports.title: American Affair flies the flag for Goldie at Goodwood
Sports.content:
Scottish speedball American Affair bounced back to form to claim top honours in the King George Qatar Stakes at Goodwood.

Jim Goldie's stable star won the King Charles III Stakes at Royal Ascot last summer, but missed the remainder of the 2025 season through injury.

A second-place finish behind the reopposing Night Raider in Haydock's Temple Stakes in May suggested he retained a good level of his ability, but having trailed home last of all when defending his Ascot title and since come up short in a Listed race at York, he was a 12-1 shot for his latest Group Two assignment.

Always up with the pace in the group that raced closest to the stands rail, American Affair finished off strongly in the hands of his regular partner Paul Mulrennan to get up and beat Rumstar and Time For Sandals down the middle of the track, with Australian raider Asfoora running her best race for a while in fourth.

Goldie senior stayed closer to home, but his son, George, said: "My dad is at Musselburgh, we couldn't both come here, but I think he'll be sorry to have missed out!

"My daughter rides him every day, he's a lovely-natured horse and he's obviously very talented.

"We had faith he'd be back to this level, we've been happy with him at home but things were interrupted by the injury he had at the back end of last year.

"This year it has been a case of building him back up to his best, he showed a glimmer at Haydock three runs ago, but Ascot was a bit of a disaster - he just pulled too hard.

"He ran well at York when he was drawn badly, so we were coming here very hopeful. He's been getting back into that flow of racing properly and finishing his race off.

"We were hoping today was going to suit him better, we were coming here very hopeful."

On future plans, he added: "The plan is to go for the Nunthorpe now, then maybe the Curragh or he could go up to six (furlongs) for the Haydock Sprint Cup.

"We've not entered him in the Abbaye, the Flying Five at the Curragh after the Nunthorpe is more likely."

Weighing-room stalwart Mulrennan said: "He's done everything right today so, touch wood, he comes back from this good. We'll enjoy today, but we've got the Nunthorpe and possibly America would be nice.

"At this stage of the game I've probably got more years behind me than in front of me, but I feel I'm still going strong. It's very competitive, it's hard. I've only got one ride down here this week, but we've made it count.

"I've got my driver with me, Adele (wife). The last time I won it was on Moviesta, Adele drove me then. I've won this race twice and I probably should have won it twice again - Easton Angel probably should have won and Moviesta another year was unlucky, so it's been an unlucky race for me and a lucky race for me, but we got it right today."

Wendy McGrandles of Barraston Racing, who own American Affair with Goldie, said: "He's had one or two excuses and we always felt that he was as good as he was last year. It's once in a lifetime for us, small breeders.

"I remember him as a foal and thinking we could maybe send him eventing if he wasn't fast enough to go racing. He was broken in to go eventing because we weren't sure whether he would be big enough or fast enough to be a racehorse. He can always do that as a second career!"

Burke eyes American trip for Shayem after Thoroughbred success

Karl Burke is eyeing a trip to America with Shayem after he denied the fast-finishing favourite Talk Of New York in the HKJC World Pool Thoroughbred Stakes.

Having finished third behind Wednesday's Sussex Stakes one-two Bow Echo and Gstaad in the St James's Palace at Royal Ascot, this Group Three contest looked a gilt-edged opportunity for Charlie Appleby's Talk Of New York to get back on the winning trail and he was priced up accordingly as the 2-5 market leader.

But while his stablemate Catullus was deployed in a pacemaking role in an attempt to ensure a sound gallop, the favourite was still keen during the early exchanges under William Buick and it then took him a while to find top gear once asked to close the gap.

Karl Burke's Shayem - winner of the Listed Sir Henry Cecil Stakes at Newmarket three weeks ago - was always in the prime position behind Catullus and after grabbing the lead racing inside the final half-furlong, he had enough in hand to keep Talk Of New York at bay by half a length in the hands of Clifford Lee.

"We don't have to lead, but we knew Billy (Loughnane, riding Catullus) was going to go off a nice gallop and Cliff was the only one really to keep tabs on the leader," said Burke.

"Last year, you would have said that he was a soft ground horse but he has proven otherwise this year. We had no qualms about the ground or the track as he handled the undulations at Newmarket well.

"Cliff is very good with his fractions. It was a great performance and Abdulrazaq (Mohamdi, owner) will be delighted as he's a homebred horse as well. He's a great supporter of ours from Dubai.

"There is a nice race at Kentucky Downs for him in September and one at Colonial Downs as well. I don't think they are Grade Ones but they are very valuable races and if if we don't go there, we could come back for the Celebration Mile."

Appleby will let the dust settle on Talk Of New York's disappointing defeat before considering his next move.

He said: "At the top of the hill I thought they'd have to go a bit to go past the lead horse because he's no mug and he likes the track. Stretching to the mile was always going to be the undoing of Catullus - stop the clock a furlong out and we were a comfortable winner.

"William said himself, the front two stole a good march on him and they're two sensible horses. We knew that Catullus was not going to see the mile out eventually but Will said 'I was only just getting rolling there the last furlong'

"I'm not using the track as an excuse, I think the winner is sensible and is improving, he's done everything right, got a nice lead from us and used it, and we've gone and finished the race off.

"You could say do we need to step up in trip? Possibly. But he has got to learn to settle a little bit as well - that first furlong he does want to be a little bit aggressive, but I don't think that was really the undoing of the race to be fair. The pace was on and they weren't coming back at the end of the day."

Sports.title: Doyle: Owen can Dream big in the Stewards' Cup
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Racing ambassador Hollie Doyle reveals her thoughts on the big handicap of the day on Saturday, the Stewards’ Cup at Goodwood.

Dream chance for Owen in Stewards' Cup

Twenty-eight runners rampaging down the hill at Goodwood in one of the most famous handicaps in world racing is a sight to savour and this weekend's Coral Stewards' Cup Handicap (3.35) certainly lives up to expectations.

It's anyone's race but I cannot get away from James Owen's likely favourite Far Above Dream who has the form, the track experience, and the draw in his favour. The four-year-old ran a career-best to finish a close fourth in the Wokingham, just behind his talented stable mate Soldier's Tree, after scoring over this course and distance in May.

He has progressed up the handicap but can race off the same mark as he did at The Royal Meeting and can prove his liking for the cut and thrust of a big field handicap for an upwardly mobile trainer.

All-Weather winner has solid course form

Another on my shortlist for the Stewards' Cup is Ollie Sangster's Tuco Salamanca - an exciting ride for young Irish ace Dylan Browne-McMonagle.

Though his recent wins have been achieved on the All-Weather, including in good company at Newcastle last month, he does have solid course form to his name and has a handy middle draw.

In last weekend's blog I put up Charles Hills's lightly raced seven-year-old Mitbaahy as my 'Hot Shot' so won't be surprised if he makes the frame at big odds on the back of that second in the Group Three Hackwood Stakes at Newbury.

Star to deny Waardah a second win in Langtry

Santorini Star has the class and the constitution to add the Group Two Qatar Lillie Langtry Stakes (3.00) on Saturday to her Group Two victories in the Park Hill Stakes at Doncaster and the Jockey Club Stakes at Newmarket.

William Haggas's five-year-old had a rare blip in the Hardwicke Stakes at Royal Ascot but this is an ideal assignment for a mare who stays well and, crucially, has winning form at the track.

Her closest market rival will be the Owen Burrows-trained Waardah, who won this race last year and found only subsequent Group One Pretty Polly Stakes Winner Estrange too good in a Group Three at Carlisle last time. She is entitled to come on for her first outing since last Autumn, but Santorini Star's overall profile is more compelling.

Three in a row for veteran Al Aasy

William Haggas holds the key to the Group Three Coral Glorious Stakes (2.25) on Saturday with market leaders Al Aasy and Opportunity, but I am expecting the veteran to win this race for the third year in a row.

Tom (Marquand) will be looking to smuggle him into the race, just as Jim Crowley did 12 months ago, and can expect another committed performance from Shadwell's wonderful Sea The Stars gelding.

Seemingly as good as ever and proven on the track, he can get the better of Wathnan Racing's Duke Of Edinburgh Stakes hero Opportunity who took his form to a new level at Royal Ascot but needs to find more on this step back into Group company.

O'Brien gelding can build on Royal Ascot form

Godolphin's Valedictory will be well supported in the Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (1.50) on Saturday, and rightly so, but I am taking him on with Irish raider Aeronautic, who can improve on his third in the race last year.

Joseph O'Brien's five-year-old struck me as a winner waiting to happen when finishing fourth in the Copper Horse Stakes at the Royal Meeting. He hasn't won for a long time but has proven he can be highly competitive off this mark of 97.

Valedictory won over course and distance in May when he was transformed by the cheekpieces but a three-pound rise for a narrow win at Newmarket last time demands more from John and Thady Gosden's gelding.

Another to consider is Charlie Johnston's Northumberland Plate Victor Align The Stars who took this prize two years ago but has never won off a triple digit rating.

Time for talented Jack to shine

Promising apprentice Jack Nicholls can make a name for himself in the Phase Eight Handicap (4.10) on Saturday when he partners Naval Light for his in-form boss Karl Burke.

The three-year-old carries a relatively low weight and Jack's three-pound claim can give him a decisive edge in this higher grade following wins at Pontefract and Catterick this summer.

Startled has been running well for Richard Hughes who has enlisted another talented claimer in Harry Vigors for this assignment. He looks fairly treated on his course and distance second in May so should be in the mix.

Billy was just brilliant on stunning Echo

Bow Echo produced the performance of the week at the Qatar Goodwood Festival, showing a blistering turn of foot to win the Group One Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes (4.10, Wednesday) and extend his unbeaten record to six.

He's clearly a very special talent - a comment that applies to his young jockey Billy Loughnane, who has shown a maturity beyond his years on George Boughey's superstar.

It takes a special horse to get out of the kind of difficult situation he found himself in on the Downs but a top-class jockey to execute a victory as Billy did so coolly. It was a great ride that will live long in the memory of racing fans and one I thoroughly enjoyed watching.

Oxygen chamber is helping my recovery

Since coming out of hospital following my fall in May, I've been using a hyperbaric oxygen chamber which we've had installed at home, and the results are encouraging.

The chamber basically increases air pressure to deliver pure one hundred per cent oxygen into your bloodstream which helps with healing. Sitting in there for an hour a day has become part of my rehabilitation routine now.

I'm also continuing with my gym programme and physiotherapy at Oaksey House in Lambourn five days a week but still don't have any idea of a comeback date at this stage.

Sports.title: Newcastle to appoint Jaissle as new boss after Howe exit confirmed
Sports.content:
Newcastle are set to announce Matthias Jaissle as their new head coach on Saturday after Eddie Howe's exit was confirmed.

Sky Sports News can reveal Newcastle have agreed to pay £9.5m (€11m) compensation to Saudi side Al Ahli for Jaissle.

The German, who previously managed Red Bull Salzburg, will sign a four-year contract at St James' Park.

The plan is for the 38-year-old to meet up with his new players in Spain on Saturday at their training camp in La Manga.

Jaissle's imminent appointment comes after Newcastle officially announced Howe's departure on Friday, a day after Sky Sports News had revealed his exit.

The reason the Howe statement was held up was to allow the club to ensure the Jaissle deal was agreed.

Jaissle's first match in charge will be a pre-season friendly against Valencia at the Mestalla next Saturday.

Howe steps down 'to recharge and take a break'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Redknapp backs former Newcastle head coach Eddie Howe to get back into management at a 'top club'.

Howe says managing Newcastle has been the privilege of his life after confirming he had stepped down as head coach.

The 48-year-old ended the Magpies' 70-year wait for domestic silverware with Carabao Cup glory in 2025, as well as overseeing qualification for the Champions League twice.

The Premier League club confirmed his exit on Friday afternoon, saying they had accepted his decision to step down and thanked him for his "extraordinary contribution".

Departing Howe said in a lengthy statement: "After a period of personal reflection, I have decided that now is the right time for me to step away from my role as head coach of Newcastle United.

"After nearly five years of giving my life, heart and soul into the club with unrelenting energy, I feel that it is in the best interests of both myself and the club to step away, recharge and take a break.

"Although it's been incredibly difficult to make this decision, I know in my heart that it's the right one. I have always put the best interests of Newcastle before my own in every single decision I have made whilst I've been here and this one is no different.

"It has been the privilege of my lifetime to have been the manager of Newcastle United.

"It is difficult to put into words what this club, the city and its supporters mean, and will always mean, to me and my family."

Howe's heartfelt 547-word message reflected on the highs and lows of his time in the north east, where he created memories that he will "cherish for the rest of my life".

Newcastle chief executive David Hopkinson added: "Eddie and his staff leave with the deep gratitude and respect of everyone at Newcastle United, and with a lasting place in the club's history.

"While we are naturally disappointed to see Eddie leave, we remain immensely thankful for everything he has done for the club.

"On behalf of our owners, board, players, staff and supporters, I would like to extend sincere thanks to Eddie for his outstanding service and leadership, and wish him and his family every success and happiness for the future."

Howe is followed out of St James' Park by coaches Jason Tindall, Graeme Jones, Stephen Purches and Simon Weatherstone, as well as head of performance Dan Hodges.

'King of this club!' - Guimaraes posts Howe farewell message

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Redknapp believes Bruno Guimaraes can benefit from Eddie Howe leaving Newcastle

Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes has called Howe the 'king of this club' following the head coach's exit.

Howe's resignation comes amid Arsenal's interest in Guimaraes, who has praised his former boss.

In an Instagram post, Guimaraes wrote the words over a picture of Howe: "King of this club!!

"Thanks for everything you've done for us. I loved enjoying our time together. Thanks for making me a better player and person!

"No words I can say will really say how much I enjoyed being your player. "Wish you all the very best in your future, gaffer."

Hornicek to be first-choice goalkeeper after £25.7m deal agreed

Image: Lukas Hornicek is set to join Newcastle from Braga

Newcastle have an agreement in principle with Braga for Lukas Hornicek, who is being brought in to be the club's first-choice goalkeeper.

Newcastle have agreed to activate his £25.7m (€30m) release clause, and are now discussing payment terms with the Portuguese club.

The 24-year-old Czech has been given permission to travel for a medical, as the two clubs tie up the loose ends of a deal.

He will become their fifth signing of the summer, taking the spending to £140m.

Sports.title: Young shoots dazzling 61 to take share of Rocket Classic lead
Sports.content:
World No 3 Cameron Young surged into a share of the lead of the Rocket Classic after a nine-under 61 in the second round in Detroit.

Young climbed 68 spots to move to 10 under with his bogey-free round and shares a three-way lead with Patrick Cantlay and Patrick Fishburn.

The two-time Open runner-up made seven birdies on his front nine and threatened to become just the second player, after Jim Furyk, to shoot two career sub-60 rounds.

"It felt like I had a 10-footer for birdie on pretty much every hole. I made a bunch of them in a row on my first nine," said Young.

"Then the putter kind of went cold a little bit for my second nine. Just really solid golf all the way through. Happy to have kind of played my way back in the tournament a little bit after Thursday."

Young is now favourite heading into the weekend and will look to continue his great recent form that saw him finish runner-up at The Open two weeks ago.

Image: Cameron Young is in the joint lead at the halfway point of the Rocket Classic (AP Photo/Jose Juarez)

The 29-year-old won The Players Championship and Cadillac Championship earlier this year but has not been able to put together a string of strong results.

"You wonder am I missing something, why is this the way that it is, why is it not working, all those things. But when it goes well, it feels totally the opposite," said Young.

"When it goes well, it feels like you never will play bad again. It just comes and goes. You kind of have to be ready for either one.

"At some point it's going to get harder and at some point you'll come out of that difficult period and it will feel easy again. It's kind of just a game of being ready for whatever comes next."

Young will fancy his chances against Cantlay and Fishburn but there are 17 other players within three shots of the lead.

England's Matt Wallace is only one shot behind after his bogey-free round of 64 and Rickie Fowler is on the same overall score of nine under.

First-round leader Peter Malnati was unable to repeat his heroics from Thursday as he made one-over 71 but is one of eight players only two shots back, including two-time major champion Xander Schauffele.
