Ememobong accused INEC of failing to maintain neutrality in matters concerning the PDP, alleging that the electoral body had repeatedly ignored material facts and court orders favourable to the party.

“The Commission’s filings, its arguments before the courts, and its refusal to comply with court orders favourable to our party have collectively created an impression of institutional bias that should concern every Nigerian,” he said.

The spokesman further argued that if INEC eventually publishes names different from those submitted by the faction, it would reinforce public concerns about the commission’s impartiality and suggest support for individuals seeking to weaken the opposition.

The faction urged its members and supporters not to lose confidence should such a scenario arise, insisting that it would continue to pursue legal and constitutional remedies.

Ememobong described the dispute as part of a broader struggle to prevent what he termed the erosion of opposition politics and the emergence of a one-party state.

He maintained that the faction’s candidates had expressed confidence in the ongoing legal process and remained committed to reclaiming the party.

“Notwithstanding INEC’s refusal to provide us with the necessary access codes, we have successfully submitted, manually and in full compliance with the Electoral Act 2026, the list of candidates sponsored by the authentic Peoples Democratic Party,” he stated.

He warned against what he called “electoral authoritarianism”, saying democratic institutions must not be used to suppress opposition parties.

Ememobong expressed optimism that the courts would ultimately resolve the leadership dispute in the faction’s favour, declaring that its members were prepared to continue the legal battle to the end.

World.title: 2027: INEC to Release Personal Particulars of Tinubu, Atiku, Obi, Others Today
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

In line with the revised time table and schedule of activities for the 2027 general election, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) will today publish the personal particulars of presidential and National Assembly candidates.

The electoral body had fixed August 1, 2026 for the display of the personal particulars of candidates for the presidential and National Assembly elections.

The leading presidential candidates include Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC); Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Peter Obi of Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC).

In line with Section 29(3) of the Electoral Act, the academic credentials and other documents submitted by candidates would be released today by INEC for public scrutiny.

Section 29(3) stipulates that: “The Commission shall, within 21 days of the receipt of the personal particulars of the candidate, publish same in the constituency where the candidate intends to contest the election.”

While the publication of candidates’ particulars is a statutory requirement designed to promote transparency in the electoral process, it also provide Nigerians with the opportunity to scrutinise the documents submitted by aspirants before the elections.

With the publication of personal details of the candidates today, political parties would officially commence campaigns for the 2027 presidential election on August 19.

NEDC: Over 60% of Roads, Bridges Destroyed By Boko Haram in Northeast Now Functional

Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

The North East Development Commission (NEDC) yesterday revealed that over 60 per cent of road infrastructure and bridges destroyed by Boko Haram insurgency in the North East are now functional.

The Managing Director of NEDC, Mohammed Alkali disclosed this during a press conference in Abuja.

Alkali explained that Phase one of the NEDC mandate was the stabilisation and recovery phase, while Phase two is the Renewal Phase; Phase three is Expansion phase and Phase four is sustainable growth.

He added that for phase one, their effort was focused on restoring critical infrastructure, supporting displaced communities, rebuilding schools, health facilities, improving security through strategic intervention, and restoring basic public services.

Mohammed revealed that it has delivered over 300 kilometres of roads and more than 50 bridges, restoring critical transport corridors, improving access to education and healthcare, facilitating trade, and strengthening regional integration.

He noted that across Adamawa State, the Commission constructed the 32km Dabna road, the Federal College of Education, Yola Road, the College of Education, Hong Road, the Garkida Cross–Kukurtu Road, and rehabilitated roads in Fufore.

Mohammed said the commission also constructed Numan Bridge, Bole Bridge, Madagali and Michika Bridges, and the Mubi–Maiha–Sarao Bridges have significantly improved connectivity, agricultural transportation and cross-border trade.

He stated: “In Bauchi State, the Commission delivered the 32km Kirfi–Gombe Abba Road, the landmark Tashan Turmi, Bara and Kalajanga Bridges, the Ningi–Yadagungume– Fuskar Mata Road, the Soro–Ganjuwa Bridge, and extensive erosion control and drainage works, improving inter-state connectivity and climate resilience.

“In Borno State, major interventions include the Ngom–Koshebe–Zabarmari– Gongulong–Khadamari Road Corridor, the Zabarmari–Dusuman Road, the reconstruction of the Gongulong–Khadamari and Monguno–Maiduguri Roads, the Fogori (Galtimari) Bridge, the Moro-Moro Market Bridge, and the Kaleri– Moduganari Bypass Road, restoring critical infrastructure destroyed by conflict and flooding.

“In Gombe State, investments including the 21km Gombe Abba–Kirfi Road, bridges along the Gombe Northern Bypass, Gombe–Dukku, Gombe–Akko and Tsando Roads, together with major erosion control works, have strengthened mobility and regional connectivity.

“In Taraba State, the rehabilitation of the Jalingo–Wukari Highway, construction of the Mayo Ndaga, Namnai and River Bantaje Bridges, alongside emergency repairs to the Mayo Kam Bridge and drainage works on the Suntai–Donga Road, have reconnected communities and improved access to agricultural and commercial centres.”

The managing-director noted that in Yobe State, the Commission delivered the 54km Mutai–Ngalda Road, the Damaturu–Buni Yadi–Magza Road Overlay, roads serving the NEDC Mega School, Potiskum.

He further disclosed that the commission constructed Damaturu–Gujba Bridge, and several bridges, culverts and drainage structures across Potiskum, Tarmuwa, Gujba and Fune Local Government Areas, enhancing mobility and flood resilience.

Mohammed added that the Governing Board approved a N100 billion investment for the deployment of 50mw of renewable energy through solar mini-grids and distributed energy systems.

According to him, “This investment builds on the success of the Commission’s Light Up the North-East Project, under which over 100,000 solar-powered street lights have been installed across the region, improving public safety, extending business hours and demonstrating the transformative impact of renewable energy on communities.”

Mohammed said the approval was also informed by the region’s significant electricity access deficit.

He stressed that while Nigeria currently records an estimated 58 per cent national electrification rate, leaving 42 per cent of the population without access to electricity, saying the challenge is considerably greater in the North-East, where only 39 per cent of the population is electrified, leaving 61 per cent without reliable access to electricity.

Mohammed lamented that this energy gap continues to limit industrial growth, agricultural processing, access to quality healthcare and education, digital inclusion and private sector investment.

World.title: NNPC’s June Profit Rose 16% to N535bn, Statutory Transfers Hit N6.29trn
World.content:
*Seplat posts 498% rise in H1 profit, set to sell 10% stake to national oil company

Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja

The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) recorded a Profit After Tax (PAT) of N535 billion in June, up from N462 billion in May, representing an increase of about 16 per cent month-on-month.

This comes as Seplat Energy Plc also released its financial performance for the first half of 2026, with PAT soaring by 498 per cent year-on-year to $164 million, buoyed by stronger crude oil prices, improved production and robust operational performance.



The NNPC in its monthly report summary released yesterday stated that its cumulative statutory payments to the federation also rose to N6.286 trillion in the first six months of this year, while total revenue increased from N4.335 trillion in May to N4.389 trillion in June.

A THISDAY analysis of the report indicated that the jump of total remittances from N4.858 trillion recorded in May to N6.286 trillion in June reflected an additional N1.428 trillion transferred during the month.



Operationally, crude oil and condensate production was 1.72 million barrels per day in June from 1.73 million bpd in May, while natural gas production increased from 7,774 million standard cubic feet per day (mmscf/d) in May to a 7,841 mmscf/d in June.

Besides, gas sales improved marginally to 4,970 mmscf/d in June from 4,921 mmscf/d in May, reversing the slight decline recorded in the previous month.



In terms of downstream operations, the data showed that petrol availability across NNPC Retail Limited stations declined to 53 per cent in June from 57 per cent in May.

The also report showed further progress on major gas infrastructure projects, as the Obiafu-Obrikom-Oben (OB3) gas pipeline project advanced from 97 per cent completion in May to 98 per cent in June, with the final tie-in works on the River Niger crossing ongoing to ensure first gas in August 2026.



Also, the NNPC announced that the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) gas pipeline remained at 94 per cent completion, with stakeholder collaboration being sustained to expedite construction and installation activities towards achieving early gas delivery to Abuja.

Meanwhile, Seplat Energy Plc has released its financial performance for the first half of 2026, with PAT soaring by 498 per cent year-on-year to $164 million, buoyed by stronger crude oil prices, improved production and robust operational performance.



Seplat also announced that it had reached an agreement to sell a 10 per cent interest in the NNPCL-SEPNU Joint Venture (JV) to the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) in a transaction valued at $281.6 million.

According to the company, the NNPC deal, expected to close in the second half of the year, would significantly enhance shareholder returns, with total planned dividends for 2026 projected to rise to 68.3 cents per share, equivalent to about $410 million and representing a 173 per cent increase year-on-year.



The indigenous energy company, listed on both the Nigerian Exchange (NGX) and the London Stock Exchange (LSE), also recorded a 30 per cent increase in revenue to $1.82 billion from $1.398 billion in the corresponding period of 2025, while cash generated from operations climbed 29 per cent to $985.9 million.



The company declared a total interim dividend of 12 US cents per share for the second quarter of 2026, comprising a core dividend of 5 cents and a special dividend of 7 cents, marking its highest-ever quarterly dividend payout.

Average production during the period rose 4 per cent to 139,509 barrels of oil equivalent per day (boepd), from 134,492 boepd recorded in the first half of 2025. The output remains comfortably within Seplat’s full-year production guidance of between 135,000 and 155,000 boepd.



In the same vein, working interest production comprised 99,518 barrels of oil per day and 182.9 million standard cubic feet of gas per day during the review period.

Second-quarter production strengthened further, averaging 149,070 boepd, representing a 9 per cent increase compared to the corresponding period of last year and a 15 per cent improvement over the first quarter of 2026.



The company attributed the improved output to stronger production from its West, East and Elcrest assets, continued success of its idle well restoration programme and higher natural gas liquids (NGLs) production.

In the same vein, gross profit surged 68 per cent to $815.9 million from $484.6 million a year earlier, while adjusted Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA) rose 28 per cent to $939 million.

Also, earnings per share climbed 565 per cent to 26.6 cents from 4.0 cents recorded in the corresponding period of 2025.

Seplat maintained a strong balance sheet, ending June with cash at bank of $433.8 million, excluding restricted cash of $130.8 million. Net debt fell by 45 per cent to $370.7 million from $673.3 million at the end of 2025, reducing its net debt-to-EBITDA ratio to 0.25 times from 0.53 times.

The company also strengthened its financial standing by repaying and cancelling $200 million under its Advanced Payment Facility (APF), leaving an outstanding balance of $100 million.

On the operational sustainability front, Seplat said its operated assets delivered 18.8 million man-hours without a Lost Time Injury (LTI), while group carbon emissions intensity declined 18 per cent year-on-year to 33.5 kilogrammes of carbon dioxide per barrel of oil equivalent.

Emissions intensity from its onshore operations declined by 37 per cent following the implementation of its End of Routine Flaring programme, the company pointed out.

Commenting on the results, outgoing Chief Executive Officer, Roger Brown, said the company entered the second half of the year from a position of considerable strength.

“As I hand over leadership of Seplat, the company is stronger than ever. Production improved from the first quarter and remains on track to grow further in the second half of 2026 as temporary restrictions are lifted and planned activities are completed,” he said.

Brown noted that higher commodity prices had translated into stronger cash generation, enabling the company to reduce debt significantly while rewarding shareholders.

“Our first-half performance benefited from a supportive commodity price environment, translating into strong cash generation. Given the limited visibility on how long these elevated prices may persist, we prioritised balance sheet strength during the quarter, repaying $200 million of our outstanding APF debt, equivalent to 20 per cent of gross debt. At the same time, robust cash flows enabled us to continue enhancing shareholder returns,” he stated.

Brown added that the announced sale of the 10 per cent interest in the offshore joint venture to NNPC Limited, together with continued strong operational performance, positions Seplat to deliver one of the highest shareholder returns in its history.

He expressed confidence in the company’s future as he prepares to hand over to Effiong Okon on August 1, saying the incoming chief executive possesses the experience and operational expertise required to drive the company’s next phase of growth and value creation.

World.title: Ghana’s Govt Backs Five-year Presidential Term, Lowers Minimum Age to 35
World.content:
Ghana has finalised moves to increase presidential term to five years as well as reduce the age limit for eligibility to 35 years.

According to news monitored on AFP, the scheme had been on the front burner for a while before its acceptance thereby changing the political landscape of the West African country.

Ghana is arguably one of Africa’s leading gold and cocoa producers, and has maintained a stable democratic system since 1992.

The change emanated from the report of a committee set up by President John Dramani Mahama to review the constitution and submitted their report Thursday.

“The government has accepted the recommendation to extend the term of office of the president from four years to five years,” Justice Minister Dominic Ayine told journalists.

The committee further recommended a commensurate increase in the tenure of lawmakers of the country to tally with the term of the president to avoid a lacuna in electoral times.

Although the committee recommended lowering the minimum age for presidential candidates to 30, Ayine said the government would instead adopt 35.

The Constitution Review Committee said a four-year presidential cycle can leave an administration with “a little over two years” of effective governing time, as the first six months can be taken up by appointments and the final year by elections.

It said a five-year term could also “strengthen democratic accountability” by giving governments more time to deliver.

A national referendum in 2027 will be required to pass the changes, with strict voter turnout and approval thresholds.

World.title: Soyinka, Chidoka, Others Demand End to Impunity, Urge Nigerians to Reclaim the State
World.content:
Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

Nobel Laureate, Prof. Wole Soyinka, former Minister of Aviation, Chief Osita Chidoka, and former Managing Director of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), Timi Alaibe, have called for a national rebirth anchored on accountability, justice and civic courage.

They insisted that Nigeria cannot overcome its governance challenges without ending impunity and restoring respect for human life.

The call was made yesterday, at the 28th Wole Soyinka Lecture Series and National Association of Seadogs (NAS) Martyrs’ Day in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, where Chidoka delivered the keynote lecture on the theme, ‘Reclaiming the Nigerian State through Accountability, Justice and Civic Courage’.

Speakers at the event agreed that their experience underscored the need to build a Nigerian state where no citizen would again suffer arbitrary abuse of power.

In his remarks, Soyinka said the gathering was dedicated to victims of state brutality, extrajudicial killings and mob violence, stressing that the value of every human life must remain the foundation of any democratic society.

He lamented what he described as the growing culture of impunity, citing the killing of a young man by a police officer, the murder of Deborah Yakubu by a mob, and the 1997 “F-18” incident involving members of NAS.

“The life of a human being constitutes the basic unit of any community and any system of governance,” Soyinka said, urging Nigerians to demand justice for victims of abuse and ensure that perpetrators are held accountable.

He also challenged authorities to reopen unresolved cases of extrajudicial killings and political assassinations, asking: “What happened to all the files of unsolved killings? We want to know why they happened and ensure justice does not fail us again.”

Delivering the keynote address, Chidoka argued that Nigeria’s greatest challenge was not the absence of laws but the failure to enforce them impartially.

According to him, the country operates an “alibi culture”, where officials explain away failures instead of accepting responsibility.

“Nigeria’s crisis is not that the state is weak; it is selectively strong. It is strong when collecting from citizens but weak when delivering services. Strong when coercing but weak when explaining,” he said.

Using the 1997 detention of 33 NAS members, popularly known as the F-18, and the 2005 Apo Six killings as examples, Chidoka said successive governments had retained the oppressive instincts of the state despite the return to democracy.

He maintained that accountability must go beyond explanations and audits to include correction, restitution and sanctions.

“Explanation without correction is not accountability,” he declared, insisting that public officials who abuse power must be identified and held personally responsible for their actions.

Chidoka also dismissed suggestions that restructuring alone would solve Nigeria’s problems, arguing that while constitutional reforms remained important, the country urgently needed a shared moral consensus built on equal citizenship, answerable leadership and justice.

He called for stronger protection for whistleblowers, respect for court orders, transparent governance and reforms to end prolonged pre-trial detentions, noting that over 64 per cent of inmates in Nigerian correctional facilities were awaiting trial.

Earlier, Alaibe said sustainable development could not thrive where accountability was absent and institutions remained weak.

Drawing from his experience in public service and regional development, he urged Nigerians to move beyond rhetoric and embrace responsible leadership.

“Nations are not reclaimed by rhetoric alone. They are reclaimed when conscience triumphs over convenience, when institutions are stronger than individuals, and when citizens summon the courage to do what is right, even when it is difficult,” he said.

Alaibe paid glowing tribute to Soyinka on his 92nd birthday, describing him as a symbol of principled patriotism whose lifelong commitment to justice continued to inspire generations of Nigerians.

Dr. Joseph Oteri, NAS Capn’s had earlier informed that the lecture formed part of activities marking NAS Martyrs’ Day, commemorating members who were detained for 72 days during the military era after being falsely labelled as opponents of the then Abacha regime.

World.title: Kim Kardashian’s daughter North West cancels her 14-date ‘Kimokawaii Tour’
World.content:
Just days before her 14-date Kimokawaii Tour, Kim Kardashian and Kanye West’s daughter, North West, has pulled the plug on the tour.

West was going to take the stage with her friend, rapper Molly Santana.

Scheduled to start on 5 August and end on 27 August, the 13-year old musician made the announcement on her Instagram without giving a reason.



According to NBC News, West wrote on her Instagram story: “I was really excited to go on tour w Molly Santana. Sadly it isn’t happening anymore.” No further details were offered.

The tickets for the shows were priced from $51, but are no longer on sale.

West released her debut EP, N0rth4evr in May.

No stranger to live stage performance, she performed with her father in front of 70,000 fans when he made a return on stage for his Los Angeles show on 1 April.

She helped him perform Talking and Piercing on My Hand.



Her first performance with her father was when she was six years old. She took the mic at the Sunday Service event in Detroit on September 27, 2019.

World.title: Dream debut! Mofokeng scores winning penalty to lift Belgian Super Cup
World.content:
Relebohile Mofokeng announces himself with winning penalty as Union Saint-Gilloise lift Belgian Super Cup

Bafana Bafana star Relebohile Mofokeng enjoyed a dream start to life at Royal Union Saint-Gilloise, scoring the winning penalty as his side defeated fierce rivals Club Brugge to win the Belgian Super Cup on Friday evening.

Making his first official appearance for the club, the 21-year-old was introduced shortly after the hour mark with Union trailing 1-0.



Kevin Mac Allister equalised in the 77th minute to force the match into a penalty shoot-out after neither side could find a winner in regulation time.

With the pressure at its highest, Mofokeng stepped up to take Union’s fifth penalty. The South African international showed remarkable composure, confidently firing his spot-kick into the top corner to seal a 5-4 shoot-out victory and hand his new club the first trophy of the season.

Mofokeng a hero for new team

It was the perfect debut for the former Orlando Pirates star, who has already become a fan favourite following his move to Belgium. Mofokeng has quickly settled into his new surroundings and continues to impress both supporters and teammates.

The Belgian Super Cup is also the eighth trophy of Mofokeng’s career, an impressive achievement for a player still only 21 years old.

Union Saint-Gilloise now turn their attention to the UEFA Champions League qualifying playoffs on Tuesday, where Mofokeng is expected to play another important role as the Belgian champions chase a place in Europe’s premier club competition.

Will Rele win more trophies?

World.title: Five children among 12 Zimbabweans killed in SA bus crash
World.content:
A deadly bus crash on South Africa's N1 highway claimed the lives of Zimbabweans. Image via X@TheTruthPanther

Five children were among 12 Zimbabweans killed when a bus travelling from Cape Town to Zimbabwe overturned on the N1 highway in South Africa’s Free State province on Wednesday evening.

The crash happened about 24 kilometres north of Trompsburg as the bus was travelling towards Edenburg.

Authorities said the vehicle was carrying about 78 passengers when it overturned.



At least 66 passengers survived the crash but sustained injuries ranging from minor to critical.

Emergency services transported the injured to nearby hospitals for treatment.

Free State Department of Health spokesperson Mondli Mvambi said authorities had not yet formally confirmed the identities and genders of those who died.



Passengers with minor injuries received treatment at Albert Nzula Hospital in Trompsburg.

Five people suffered serious injuries, while four critically injured passengers were transferred to Pelonomi Trauma Hospital in Bloemfontein for specialised emergency care.

Bus crash investigation continues

Authorities closed the N1 in both directions following the bus crash to allow forensic pathologists to examine the scene and recovery teams to remove the wreckage.



Investigators have not yet determined what caused the accident.

Free State MEC for Community Safety Jabu Mbalula extended condolences to the families of those who lost their loved ones.

“On behalf of the Free State Provincial Government, I extend my heartfelt condolences to the families who have lost their loved ones in this tragic accident. To those injured, we wish you a speedy and full recovery. This is a devastating loss, and our thoughts are with all those affected,” he said.



Key cross-border route

The N1 is one of Southern Africa’s busiest transport corridors, linking South Africa with neighbouring countries including Zimbabwe, Zambia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Malawi, Angola and Tanzania.

Thousands of Zimbabweans use the route each year to travel between South Africa and home for work, family visits and holidays.

The highway also carries significant volumes of commercial traffic and long-distance passenger buses.



The latest crash has once again raised concerns about road safety on one of the region’s busiest cross-border routes, where several fatal bus accidents have occurred in recent years.

Zimbabwean authorities had not yet issued a statement on the tragedy at the time of publication.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs transfers: Ex-skipper, fan favourite to leave the club
World.content:
Given Msimango could move to Stellenbosch as a part of a deal that would see Langelihle Phili move to Naturena. Photo: Chiefs Facebook

Despite being a mainstay at one stage in his Kaizer Chiefs career, Given Msimango is now surplus to requirements at the club. What happened?

Msimango offered to Stellenbosch as makeweight in a deal for Phili

29-year-old central defender Given Msimango looks set to leave the club. Despite initially being a key pillar of the side after signing in 2023, the ex-TS Galaxy man has become a fringe operator. Inacio Miguel and even the now-departed Aden McCarthy moved ahead of him in the pecking order. Injuries also haven’t helped.

“SABC Sport has established that defender Given Msimango is one of two players Kaizer Chiefs have offered, together with a cash payment, to Stellenbosch FC in an effort to secure the signing of highly rated winger Langelihle Phili,” reads part of a report by SABC Sport.



Kaizer Chiefs’ five signings and what they’ll bring

Khanyisa Mayo has signed permanently from CR Belouizdad for a reported fee close to R9.8 million following a prior loan spell. Adolf Mtasingwa is a 27-year-old defensive midfielder signed from Azam FC for an undisclosed fee, and the first Tanzanian player to join Amakhosi. Mtasingwa brings valuable experience, having spent six seasons in Scandinavia, playing in the Icelandic, Norwegian and Finnish leagues. He returned home in 2024 to help Azam FC finish third in the Tanzanian league last season. He is the vice-captain of his nation.

Central defender Thabo Moloisane brings PSL know-how after becoming a mainstay for an impressive Stellenbosch side. Moloisane can also operate at right back when needed. 28-year-old goalkeeper Renaldo Leaner joins from Sekhukhune to bolster Chiefs’ options between the sticks. The 1.87m-tall stopper has been capped by Bafana. Finally, Langelihle Phili brings electric pace and directness from wide areas. The 21-year-old is expected to officially arrive from Stellies.

World.title: SASSA warning: Ignore this SMS and you could lose your grant
World.content:
SASSA has warned beneficiaries not to ignore grant review SMS notifications, saying failure to complete the review process could result in grants being suspended or lapsing. Image: Pexels

Thousands of SASSA beneficiaries are being urged not to ignore SMS notifications requesting them to attend a grant review, warning that failure to respond could result in their grant being suspended or lapsing.

The reminder comes ahead of the August payment cycle, with the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) saying beneficiaries selected for review will receive their grants on the fourth payment day, Friday, 7 August, instead of during the normal three-day payment schedule.

However, SASSA stressed that receiving a review SMS does not mean a beneficiary has done anything wrong.



Instead, grant reviews form part of the agency’s legal responsibility to ensure social assistance is paid only to people who continue to qualify.

Why SASSA sends review SMSs

According to SASSA, reviews are carried out to:

Confirm beneficiaries still qualify for their grant.

Verify information on record.

Prevent fraud and abuse.

Keep the beneficiary database up to date.

The agency sends review notifications via SMS using the cellphone number recorded on its system.

For that reason, beneficiaries are urged to keep their contact details current.

Why your cellphone number matters

SASSA warned that beneficiaries who change their cellphone number without informing the agency could miss important review notices.

The agency also expects beneficiaries to report changes to:



Residential address.

Marital status.

Financial circumstances or income.

Travel outside South Africa.

Any other information that could affect eligibility.

Keeping these details updated helps prevent unnecessary payment delays and interruptions.

What happens if you ignore the SMS?

Beneficiaries who receive a review notification should visit their nearest SASSA office during August to complete the process.

Failure to do so could result in the grant being suspended or lapsing in terms of the Social Assistance Act.

Beneficiaries who are unable to visit an office because they are bedridden or medically unfit can arrange for an authorised representative to act on their behalf.

Older Persons Grant: Tuesday, 4 August

Tuesday, 4 August Disability Grant: Wednesday, 5 August

Wednesday, 5 August Children’s Grants: Thursday, 6 August

Thursday, 6 August Grants under review: Friday, 7 August

Beneficiaries who do not receive payment during the first three payment days should first check whether their grant has been selected for review before rushing to a SASSA office.

World.title: Revised OUTLOOK for SASSA Older Person Grants in August 2026
World.content:
SASSA Older Person Grants in August 2026 will roll off this coming week, and not a moment too soon for the country’s four-million elderly. Tuesday 4 August 2026 is the day, but it’s been offset by a longer-than-usual wait time. Anyone following SASSA payment dates closely will know it has been four-and-a-half weeks, or 33 days, to be exact …

As such, recipients of SASSA Older Person Grants in August 2026 have had stretch their finances to the absolute breaking point. Many are probably sitting on bank accounts of nil with no food in their cupboards. Not ideal with bills to pay and the announcement last week that consumer inflation is at new highs in 2026, and only likely to increase.

SASSA OLDER PERSON GRANTS IN AUGUST 2026

Nevertheless, South African Social Security Agency Older Person Grants were authorised to increase by a miserly R80 back in April 2026, and they will pay the following this month:



SASSA Old-Age Grants 60 to 74 years old – R2 400 (up from R2 320)

(up from R2 320) SASSA Old-Age Grants 75 years and older – R2 420 (up from R2 340)

While there is no confirmation on official October 2026 increases, it did emerge that the Department of Social Development (DSD) has underspent R4.8 billion over the last financial year on grants. By our calculations, that differential, split across all four-million state-sponsored pensioners, could pay as much as an extra R100 per month for a full year. While unlikely to be that high, this could spell some good news for a worthwhile interim increase in October 2026.

ARE STRICT REVIEWS HELPING OR HURTING THE ELDERLY?

The vast majority of pensioners have no money or food left by the end of the grant payment cycle. Image: File

This revised outlook ahead of SASSA Older Person Grants in August 2026 does raise some important questions over agency management. It has put in place . According to the agency, over time, it has targeted more than 300 000 suspect profiles and saved more than R170 million thanks to the process.

However, these savings are a drop in the ocean compared to billions in unspent funds due to maladministration. President Ramaphosa fired minister Sisisi Tolashe and replaced her with Dina Pule this month. The former minister left office in disgrace 13 years ago following a corruption scandal in her former role.

LATEST ON SASSA TARGETED REVIEWS

As ever, beneficiaries awaiting SASSA Older Person Grants in August 2026 know all-too well of the rigours of eLife certification and eligibility review. SASSA now cross-references all banking data with a host of other government departments and banks. Therefore, anyone who has been claiming a government grant that shouldn’t be cannot hide for much longer. Worse still, if you are caught misrepresenting your means, not only will you lose your grant, but you will have to pay back the money with interest.

For those who are reviewed by SASSA and clear their names, they receive a deferred payment on a fourth date. This month, it falls on Friday 7 August 2026. However, if you cannot clear your name, you face the option of two different payment plans: One is the lumpsum payback, which is most affordable. But the vast majority end up paying back SASSA money on a layaway plan, incurring high interest rate penalties in the process.

REVISED REVIEWS SASSA OLDER PERSON GRANTS IN AUGUST 2026

The agency claims shorter queues and faster response times. But it all depends on applicants have the correct documentation with them. Image: File

To make things tougher, the agency has also increased the income (means) and asset eligibility for SASSA Older Person Grants in August 2026:



Your income must be less than R9 350 (single) or R18 700 (married) per month.

(single) or (married) per month. This adds up to R112 200 (single) or R224 400 (married) per year.

(single) or (married) per year. Total assets (property) in your name cannot be worth more than R1 584 000 (single) or R3 168 000 (married).

Here’s what you need to know and be able to show the agency when applying for SASSA Older Person Grants in August 2026:

Official RSA identity document (ID) preferably a Smart ID Card with digital ID photo.

with digital ID photo. Valid three months’ statement certified by your bank, plus copies.

statement certified by your bank, plus copies. All documents proving your marital status, plus death certificates if necessary.

Proof of residence (a utility bill with your name on it, not older than three months ).

). Documents proving your income and/or financial dividends (very important).

Comprehensive information regarding assets/valuation of any property you own.

Full declaration of any and all private pension in your name.

Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) membership book, or discharge certificate from your previous job.

A copy of your will, first and final liquidation and distribution accounts if your spouse has passed away in the last five years.

HOW LONG DOES IT TAKE TO BE APPROVED FOR SASSA OLDER PERSON GRANTS?

New applicants for SASSA Older Person Grants in August 2026 typically take around three months to be processed, but you will be back paid to the date of your first application. However, that’s if you have all your documents correct at the first time of asking. For existing clients, it is now possible to skip the queues and complete eLife certification and biometric verification at the agency’s new online service portal HERE to save time.

Plus, if you’re too old, sick or live in a remote rural area you can get a loved one to help with your SASSA Older Person Grants in August 2026 application. All you need is a letter from your doctor. And all of the above documentation copied and certified by a commissioner of oaths. If you are denied the grant you do have three months to appeal the decision with the DSD HERE.

You can try to contact SASSA directly here:

SASSA toll-free line: 0800 601 011

Head Office of SASSA: 012 400 2322

Email SASSA: grantsenquiries@sassa.gov.za

But what do you think? How did you handle the long wait to SASSA Older Person Grants in August 2026? What tips do you have for other beneficiaries to make their grants last for more than a month? Be sure to share your ideas in the comments section below …

World.title: Ratepayers Slam R11m Durban ICC Upgrade
World.content:
DURBAN - The eThekwini Ratepayers' Protest Movement has rejected the R11-million upgrade to Durban's International Convention Centre.

The move -- to urgently upgrade the toilets and other areas for the SADC summit in August -- relies on money redirected from other projects.

The eThekwini Municipality has not shared the specifics, but the plans reportedly include upgrading the toilets.

Ratepayers are not pleased.

"There's no planning that's taking place because, I mean, the ICC in itself should be undergoing regular maintenance. And had they been doing this, there wouldn't be a need for a reprioritisation of the budget," said Asad Gaffar from the eThekwini Ratepayers Protest Movement.

The Durban Chamber of Commerce and Industry believes a broader upgrade is needed.

" From a business point of view, for us to compete at an international level, to also, you know, compete for international conferences. Our conference centre needs to be up to date and it, it needs to be ready," said DCCI CEO Palesa Phili.

World.title: Mettler's suspension declared unlawful
World.content:
PRETORIA - The Pretoria High Court has lifted Tshwane City Manager Johann Mettler's suspension.

The court ruled that the special council vote to suspend him was unlawful.

The Democratic Alliance had filed an urgent court application to challenge resolutions taken during the 9 July sitting.

The party disputed the speaker's decision to exclude 13 votes from the DA and FF Plus on voting day.

Council Speaker Mncedi Ndzwanana had recorded the officials in question as being on leave.

The court found that the speaker had no authority to disregard the disputed votes.

The resolutions adopted at that meeting were set aside.

World.title: Final voter registration weekend kicks off
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - With just over 90 days before the local government elections, the IEC is urging all eligible South Africans to go out and register to vote.

This is the final voter registration weekend ahead of the November 4th polls.

All registration stations will operate from 8am until 5pm.

Over three million registrations were recorded in the first voter registration weekend.

The IEC says this reflects the citizens' continued commitment to democratic participation.

You can also register online. The commission is urging participants to use the data-free online self-service portal.

Voters are reminded to register where they currently live.

World.title: Cat cafe felines rescued after Japan quake sparks mall blast
World.content:
TOKYO - Twenty-five cats stuck inside a shopping mall in Japan gutted in an explosion after a major earthquake have been rescued, triggering huge relief on social media.

Momo, Kohaku, Tango, Shandy -- a fluffy Norwegian Forest Cat -- and the others were in Cat Cafe MOFF on the ground floor of the Aeon mall in Kashima when the deadly 7.1-magnitude quake hit on Tuesday.

The mall was evacuated and employees returned to retrieve the cats when a huge explosion -- likely caused by gas -- ripped through the building, and staff "hurriedly evacuated", the cafe said.

At least 34 people died in the quake, according to authorities in the southwestern Kumamoto region.

On Wednesday, with permission from the fire service, the police and the mall operator, MOFF's manager entered the building and safely rescue all 25 cats, which were unharmed.

Around 10:00 pm (1300 GMT) the same day, the animals arrived safely in the city of Hiroshima in western Japan, where the company has another cat cafe, it said.

"We were concerned about fatigue from the long journey from Kumamoto, but after arriving we provided individual care for each of them," it said.

It added that the cats were "spending their time quietly and calmly".

An online news article about the cats' miraculous escape posted on X by Livedoor News garnered 7.9 million views.

"People say human lives come first, but human lives and cat lives are both equally precious... I'm glad everyone's safe," said one user on Instagram.

Cat cafes -- as well as other similar establishments in Japan where people can pet anything from hedgehogs to miniature pigs -- are, however, controversial.

"If possible, I hope they won't be sent back to the cat cafe, but instead find them adoptive homes where they can live a safe and secure life surrounded by love," said another user on Instagram.

Others criticised people's focus on the animals rather than the human toll at the mall, where seven bodies were found.

World.title: Hamas agrees to disarm: What are the challenges ahead?
World.content:
GAZA CITY - Hamas said on Friday it agreed to a deal to end the war with Israel that included provisions addressing its weapons and the gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from the Gaza Strip.

The text of the agreement has not been released publicly, and there has been no official reaction from the Israeli government, but far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir said he opposed the deal.

Here are some of the challenges the deal would face on the ground in Gaza.

- Opposition -

US President Donald Trump announced the "complete disarmament" of Hamas, calling it a critical step towards a new Palestinian government in Gaza.

He said Israeli forces would withdraw from Gaza "as disarmament is completed".

Hamas officials told AFP a committee established by Trump's Board of Peace to govern Gaza would oversee the process of storing the Islamist movement's weapons.

The agreement announced by Hamas mirrors the Gaza plan proposed by Trump and endorsed by his Board of Peace, under which Hamas would disarm in exchange for a phased Israeli withdrawal.

Hours before Hamas announced the agreement, an Israeli political source told reporters that Gaza was not even discussed during Trump and Netanyahu's meeting this week in Washington.

"Israel demands the complete disarmament of Hamas, including the removal of weapons from Gaza and full demilitarisation of the Strip as a precondition for any process," the source said.

"There will be no Israeli withdrawal from the yellow line in the Gaza Strip before Hamas is disarmed and the Strip is demilitarised," they added, referring to a demarcation between the area under Hamas control and that held by the Israeli army.

On Friday, Israeli minister Ben Gvir expressed his opposition to the deal.

"The draft agreement published by the Board of Peace is unacceptable to Israel... the assassinations in Gaza must continue," he said on Telegram.

Hamas said it expected mediators and the Board of Peace to ensure Israel complied with the deal's terms, which included Israel's "gradual withdrawal" from Gaza.

"The agreement contains a clear provision stating that Israel must commit to and implement its obligations. If Israel does not implement the agreement, neither will we," Ghazi Hamad, a member of the group's negotiating team, told AFP.

However, Muhammad Shehada, a researcher at the European Council on Foreign Relations, said Netanyahu was highly unlikely to accept such terms with elections looming.

"It would amount to political suicide," he said, noting that Defence Minister Israel Katz had "even pledged to rebuild Jewish settlements there".

- Implementation and timetable -

"Our focus now turns to implementation," the Board of Peace said, adding that the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG), established by the board, will "soon begin a phased transition toward full authority".

According to Hamas, Israel's withdrawal, the deployment of an international force, the installation of NCAG and the handling of the movement's weapons must all proceed in parallel.

"What we are seeing instead is a continued expansion of the (Israeli) occupation," said Paris-based Hamas specialist Leila Seurat.

Israeli military officials say that the army controlled more than 60 percent of Gaza, more than what it did when the ceasefire was announced in October.

Hamas officials say the next two weeks will be devoted to agreeing on the mechanisms for implementing the deal.

"We must agree on every detail: how the agreement will be implemented, when it will be implemented and the mechanisms for carrying it out. This is what will take place in the coming days," said Hamad.

Seurat says Hamas's public announcements are also part of a communications strategy.

"Its main objective is to say: we are fulfilling our part of what was agreed, while Israel is doing nothing," she said.

Nickolay Mladenov, the Board of Peace's high representative for Gaza, said the implementation stage of the plan "matters even more" than the initial deal.

"Withdrawal must move in lockstep with decommissioning."

- Obstacles on the ground -

Progress will therefore depend largely on whether the mediators -- Egypt, the United States, Qatar and Turkey -- can secure agreement on both a timetable and implementation mechanisms.

They are expected to meet in Cairo shortly for that purpose.

But even if a timetable is agreed, significant practical hurdles remain.

The NCAG has yet to be allowed to enter the Gaza Strip.

The International Stabilisation Force (ISF), which is expected to support the transition and oversee the disarmament process alongside a new Palestinian police force, is also still in the process of being established.

World.title: Google rolls back new satellite image AI tool after backlash
World.content:
SAN FRANCISCO - Google rolled back a new feature allowing Google Earth users to generate AI visualisations on top of the service's satellite imagery, following a furious backlash from researchers and open-source intelligence experts about the potential for disinformation.

"We've seen geospatial professionals using this feature for a range of useful purposes, however we've also seen people sharing screenshots of generated imagery that appear to violate our policies," a Google spokesperson said in a statement to AFP. "So we're rolling back this feature in Google Earth while we work on implementing stronger guardrails."

"We know that people uniquely trust Google Earth for a reliable view of the world," the statement added.

The "create image" tool, unveiled Thursday, had integrated Google's Nano Banana 2 image-generation technology into Google Earth, letting users zoom into locations and build pictures in seconds based on the program's satellite, aerial and 3D-mapping data.

Google had described it as a way to "visualise history, create real estate plans and more."

But disinformation researchers warned that it could enable bad actors to misuse Google Earth -- a key resource for fact-checking and verification -- to create realistic geospatial fakes.

"Google spent 20 years building the reference the world checks against," digital investigations expert Henk Van Ess wrote in one widely shared post on Substack. "Today it added a button that makes things up."

Brady Africk, a research analyst at the American Enterprise Institute specialising in satellite imagery analysis, told AFP the Google Earth update would have made it "easier to generate convincing fake satellite imagery that can spread quickly online and mislead the public."

Such fakes "erode public trust in satellite imagery, and make the jobs of journalists and researchers more difficult," he said.

- 'Irrevocably damaged overnight' -

As the critiques piled up, Google had said on X that the images created with the feature included SynthID digital watermarks, invisible markers embedded in media generated using the company's artificial intelligence tools.

"We take misinformation seriously," the company wrote, linking to an AI policy that instructs users against "misinformation, misrepresentation or misleading activities."

AFP's tests of the feature on Friday were able to fabricate satellite images that could have had serious global consequences: an explosion in Paris, a nuclear site in Iran, a bomb crater in Russia and an Islamic State group training ground in Syria.

The tool also fulfilled prompts to visualise other fake scenes, including floods across Bangladesh, a migrant caravan camped at the US-Mexico border and a suspicious warehouse holding vans in Georgia -- one of several states US President Donald Trump has falsely accused of widespread election fraud.

The "create image" button no longer appeared within Google Earth after Google paused its use.

Similar fakes have previously had real-world impacts. In 2023, an AI image depicting an explosion at the Pentagon briefly rattled the markets.

Early in the US war with Iran, an AI-altered satellite image depicting a destroyed US military base garnered millions of views across platforms.

Among the groups that called for Google to reverse its decision was the London-based Centre for Information Resilience, whose executive director Ross Burley told AFP the feature was "irresponsible."

"Trust in satellite imagery has taken decades to build and could be irrevocably damaged overnight," Burley said.

GeoConfirmed, a volunteer-driven open-source intelligence project that verifies visuals from conflicts around the globe, had also urged Google to reconsider.

"We are already observing individuals exploiting the new Google Earth web tool to make military positions, relabel buildings as schools, and experiment with manipulating the information environment," the group wrote on X, before Google announced it was rolling back the feature.

"The primary, and perhaps only, practical use of this tool appears to be the creation and dissemination of mis- and disinformation."

World.title: Magaia salvages last-gasp WAFCON draw for South Africa
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Hildah Magaia scored nine minutes into added time to salvage a 2-2 draw for South Africa against Ivory Coast on Friday in the Women's Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco.

The Ivorians led 2-0 at half-time in the Group B match thanks to a brace from 18-year-old Grace Sery. Thembi Kgatlana halved the deficit midway through the second half in Casablanca.

Substitute Magaia had a goal ruled offside in added time, then ran on to a headed pass from Ronnel Donnelly and slammed the ball past goalkeeper Aramatou Diakite to snatch a point.

Ivory Coast top the table with four points. Tanzania have three, South Africa one and Burkina Faso none.

Tanzania, who struck a late winning goal against South Africa four days ago, face Burkina Faso later on Friday and will qualify for the quarter-finals if they secure maximum points.

In the final round on Tuesday, Ivory Coast face Tanzania and former champions South Africa meet Burkina Faso.

South Africa must beat the Burkinabe to have a chance of reaching the knockout phase and keeping alive hopes of a second successive World Cup appearance.

Brazil will host the global women's football showpiece in 2027 and the four WAFCON semi-finalists qualify automatically for the 32-nation tournament.

The losing WAFCON quarter-finalists will get a second chance to reach the World Cup through play-offs, first in Morocco and then in an inter-continental competition.

Sery struck on 18 and 36 minutes from assists by another 18-year-old, N'Sira Ouedraogo, to rattle sluggish South Africa, who made four changes after the loss to Tanzania.

The Ivorian teenagers both play for Danish club Nordsjaelland, and their pace and power were threats throughout the opening half.

Realising a loss would almost certainly condemn them to a shock WAFCON exit, South Africa exerted constant pressure after the break against rivals 15 places lower in the world rankings.

Kgatlana cut inside Aicha Fofana and fired past Diakate on 71 minutes to restore hope. Then Magaia levelled with the Ivorian goalkeeper once again beaten at her near post.

World.title: Is it you? Some SASSA beneficiaries to wait longer for August payout
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Some South African Social Agency (SASSA) beneficiaries will have to wait much longer for their August grant payments.

This is because they would have been among those whose profiles are under review.

SASSA, however, urged beneficiaries not to panic as they will receive their payment on 7 August.

The agency urged beneficiaries not to take this process lightly, as it will be to their detriment.

“After receiving their grant on the fourth day, beneficiers ae urged to visit their nearest SASSA offices during August to complete the review process. Failure to respond to a review may result in the grant being suspended or lapsing in accordance with the Social Assurance Act,” SASS said in a statement.

According to SASSA, those selected for the grant review have been notified through SMS.

The review process, among other reasons, aims to remove people who no longer qualify from the system, prevent fraud and abuse as well as maintain an accurate and up-to-date beneficiary database.

As such, SASSA said it is important for beneficiaries to inform its offices if there are changes to their personal circumstances.

These changes include:

Marital status

Residential or contact address

Financial circumstances or income

Travel outside of the borders of the country

Or any information that may affect grant eligibility

In the meantime, other payments are expected to roll out as scheduled with

Older Persons Grant: Tuesday, 4 August

Disability Grant: Wednesday 5 August

Children’s Grant: Thursday 6 August
