World.title: Bear cub encounters near homes prompt safety warning from experts
World.content:
Bear cubs appearing close to human habitation are not cute cuddly toys, experts have warned, and it may only be a matter of time before such incidents end up with someone being harmed, Maaleht reported .

The cautions come following several incidents, including one filmed earlier this month which went viral and which showed three bear cubs strolling around the yard of a Harju County farmhouse in full view of people.

"The truth is that even a one-and-a-half-year-old bear has claws, fangs and considerable strength, enough to inflict very serious injuries on a person if necessary. An attack by a mother bear would most likely be fatal," said Ruttar Roht, a representative of the Ardu Hunting Society – a society member had put up the original bear cubs video, adding wild animals are always unpredictable.

"The truth is that even a one-and-a-half-year-old bear has claws and fangs and quite a lot of strength, which, if necessary, can cause quite serious injuries to a person. An attack by a female bear would most likely end fatally for a person," Roht went on.

Marko Vinn, advisor to the national hunting society, said while encounters with bears in Estonia have so far ended happily for all involved, with large predators increasingly venturing into human settlements, sooner or later that happy situation may change.

How the three cubs came to be separated from their mother is unknown, with speculation including she had come to harm, had temporarily abandoned her cubs for their safety, or they had escaped from her – Vinn said this could happen if an adult male had attempted to kill the cubs in order to mate with the mother with a view to producing his own cubs, a not unheard-of scenario with bears in the wild.

While the cubs in the video are too young to viably survive without their mother over the long term, this does not mean feeding them and giving them water is an option – the animals might then become reliant on human aid, which is also unnecessary given the abundance of freshwater bodies, small and large, in Estonia.

Estonians, Vinn noted, have lost their rural roots and have become so urbanized that they have lost a clear picture of nature red in tooth and claw, tending to see the animals more as cute cuddly toys.

Roht and Vinn disagreed on the rise in bear numbers being down to clear-cutting of forests – clearing away trees wholesale – with Roht saying if anything the practice provides more opportunities for them to hunt, and so does not drive them out of the forest as has been claimed; it is simply the numbers, around 1,100 and counting, which have led to more bears, often weaker individuals, ending up nearer to human habitation than before, he said.

As omnivores, bears will happily feed on berries and fruit found in bogland and open areas, and even on agricultural produce.

The viral video shared by the Estonian Hunters' Society on July 23 showed cubs later confirmed to have returned to the forest, though one is thought to have later raided a chicken coop in Paide, prompting the Rescue Board and the Environmental Agency to relocate it.

Over the past 20 years, the bear population has almost doubled, indicating a very favorable conservation status, Maaleht reported, adding the low point in the thousands of years they have been resident in the area – since the end of the last ice age, in fact – came in the 1920s, when only around 30 animals were living in the country, and even in the 1950s the figure was below 100.

Hunters' lobby groups have been calling for an expansion to the annual bear cull, claiming numbers are now too high.

Worldwide, brown bears (Ursus arctos) number around 200,000, with an estimated 130,000 of these being in the Russian Federation. Grizzly bears are a subspecies of the brown bear.

If you see bear cubs apparently separated from their mother, you should call the national information hotline on 1247.

The Estonian Hunters' Society advises staying calm, never feeding bears, making noise while walking in forests, and avoiding bear cubs, carcasses and roaming alone. If a bear is seen near homes as in the recent events, scare it away with loud noise rather than approaching or photographing it. Keep dogs leashed, back away slowly if threatened, never run or climb a tree, and if attacked by a brown bear, lie on the ground, protect your head and neck, and play dead.

World.title: Finland to work with Estonia to stop migrants, interior minister says
World.content:
Interior Minister Igor Taro (Eesti 200) said the Finnish authorities will assist their Estonian counterparts in stopping illegal immigrants who are trying to reach the Nordics after crossing the Belarusian-Latvian border.

Over the past two weeks, over 80 migrants have been detained in Estonia, most likely after entering the European Union illegally via the Belarusian-Latvian border, as part of what authorities say is a hybrid attack orchestrated by the Minsk regime. This is a significant increase, as the total number stands at 128 detained so far this year.

The migrants have been caught in hotels, Tallinn city center, and around the port. The Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) said they are mostly trying to reach Finland, as routes to Germany have become more difficult due to checks on the Polish borders.

Taro said the Estonian and Finnish authorities have reached an agreement that the Finns will come to help Estonia at ports and airports.

"Then we have a few more eyes and pairs of hands at transport hubs, and we free up a little resources to deal with hotels and accommodation facilities. Since people have been caught in shopping centres here, our Police and Border Guard Board personnel can deal with them more outside ports and airports as well," he told the "Uudis+" on Friday.

Minister of the Interior Igor Taro. Source: Siim Lõvi / ERR

He said the Finnish forces can arrive in a matter of hours.

"We need this kind of additional force. We discussed all kinds of possibilities for carrying out some kind of joint operation so that illegal immigrants would not be able to continue onwards through Finland. It would be a very bad message if they managed to get to Finland – it would mean that it is possible to go through Estonia," Taro said.

The minister added that Estonia wants to send a clear message.

"It is very important that we can catch everyone and that they do not move onwards from Estonia, so that nobody gets the impression that Estonia is a suitable transit corridor through which one can get to wherever they want to go. These are not simply migrants; things must be called by their proper names here – these are illegal immigrants. They are trying to get to Europe illegally and they have no right to do so," he stressed.

Migrants sent back to Latvia

The migrants detained in Estonia will be returned to Latvia, following EU rules, Taro said. New rotations of border guards will also be sent to assist their Latvian counterparts on the Belarus border for the next two months.

"First, we are going to help on Latvia's external border. Second, Latvia itself has been very reasonable in its approach throughout this situation, and everyone whom we have detained and who has apparently come from that direction will indeed be sent back through Latvia," Taro said.

"For our detention centres not to become overcrowded and for us not to deal with lengthy procedures here in Estonia, it is in fact very important to send all these people back," the minister added.

The Latvian-Belarusian border. Source: Latvian Border Guard.

The identification of the migrants and their country of origin will be carried out in Estonia, while further procedures take place in Latvia. The minister said there is no point in Estonia duplicating a system that already exists in Latvia.

He added that there is no reason why illegal immigrants should be allowed to remain in the European Union.

"If a person has crossed the border illegally and has also come from a safe country, I do not see any argument that we or Latvia should offer them international protection. They have not come directly from a war zone, but have travelled through safe countries," Taro said.

As of Thursday, Estonian authorities had caught five smugglers. The minister added that this number will increase.

Tense months ahead

Yesterday, more than a dozen migrants staying at a short-term rental property in the Nõmme suburb of Tallinn were detained by the PPA. The interior ministers said smugglers use both cheaper hotels and private accommodation.

"I would urge people to keep an eye on what is happening in these accommodation places. These latest detentions have all happened thanks to attentive citizens who have reported that something is wrong," Taro said.

The minister stressed that those placing the orders and those who later use the accommodation may not be the same people.

Police operation on Tallinn's Nõmme district on Thursday. Source: Private collection

"They have smugglers or helpers of illegal migrants who can arrange certain things. They book accommodation for them and afterwards completely different people come in, so it is worth keeping an eye on things," Taro said.

He called on Estonian residents to be vigilant.

"I have repeatedly said that if Estonian residents see some strange group of foreigners who look lost and do not know exactly where they are going. They are clearly not cruise tourists, then such people should definitely be reported," he said.

"I cannot be ruled out that more will be caught somewhere again. I predict that perhaps for up to a couple of months we may have a very tense and difficult period," Taro said "Uudis+".

World.title: Kuressaare begins chlorinating water after E. coli found in routine tests
World.content:
Kuressaare Water Utility has begun chlorinating the city's water supply after routine drinking‑water tests showed, based on preliminary lab results, E. coli and other coliform bacteria at the ends of local pipelines.

Saarte Hääl reported that the samples were taken on 30 July and that, according to Kuressaare Water Utility, the information is preliminary and the official analysis protocol has not yet been issued.

The utility recommends that residents in the Upa area boil drinking water as an additional precaution before use.

According to the company, a coli‑like bacterium is an indicator that may appear at pipeline ends during warm weather and stagnant water, and its presence mainly signals the need to flush the system.

More attention is required for the E. coli bacterium found at the end of the Upa pipeline, which has not been detected in Kuressaare's water over the past three years. The utility says that a single E. coli finding does not in itself mean the city's drinking water is widely contaminated, but it does require immediate action.

Read more in Saarte Hääl.

World.title: Tech firm Nebius hiring push fuels speculation over Estonia data center plans
World.content:
The international technology company Nebius, which develops artificial intelligence infrastructure, is recruiting employees in Tallinn, but the company's exact plans in Estonia are not known.

Nebius, an international technology company born from the restructuring of the Russian tech giant Yandex and headquartered in Amsterdam, is hiring in Estonia. The company is offering positions for a data centre IT manager, IT technician, IT support unit manager, IT infrastructure engineer and senior IT technician, and is also looking for a warehouse and logistics specialist.

Both Estonia's largest data centre Greenergy Data Centers and Sunly, which is building a data centre in Läänemaa, believe that if one major international client can be attracted to Estonia, others will gradually follow.

Since it became known this week that Greenergy Data Centers in Hüüru is building additional IT capacity to install artificial intelligence computing power and expand its client base beyond Estonia, journalists asked Greenergy whether they had struck a deal with Nebius.

Greenergy andmekeskus Hüürus. Autor/allikas: Tõnu Tunnel/Greenergy

Greenergy Data Centers' large‑client segment manager Martin Rungi did not wish to comment on the assumption, but noted that Greenergy has so far built out only a small part of its resource and that there is still a long way to go to reach the full potential of up to 300 megawatts.

"We are targeting all the names you hear in the public information space – Amazon, Microsoft, Google, they are all welcome clients. But who and when and in what volume will move here, that will be clear when the time is right. I cannot answer this question otherwise, but our ambition is to serve everyone operating in this field," Rungi said.

He added that the international market is highly supply‑constrained and Estonia has resources to offer. However, concrete agreements in this business are often not discussed publicly.

"A lot of things in our business are confidential until the parties themselves disclose them," Rungi said. "Since most clients are listed companies, they have their own rules for disclosure, and we cannot say anything until they are able to comment."

Nebius also did not provide clarification on its plans in Estonia.

Some data centre clients in Estonia will remain unknown to the public. For critical infrastructure, clients aim to keep the location of their data strictly hidden. Rungi said Greenergy is negotiating with many clients simultaneously and work is very active.

"There are always all kinds of speculations," Rungi said, adding that in this industry it is normal that information is disclosed only when a major client announces something.

Sunly kavandab Eestisse Baltimaade suurimat andmekeskust. Autor/allikas: Sunly

Sunly also actively seeks major clients

Commenting on Nebius hiring in Estonia, Rungi said that there are several development projects in Estonia, including Greenergy, Sunly and Evecon. "There is more than one bride at this wedding," he added.

Sunly, a renewable energy company planning to build the largest data centre in the Baltics in Läänemaa, did not wish to speculate on whether Nebius might target Greenergy's Hüüru data centre as a location.

Sunly's energy centre development manager Kaarel Aus said the sector is developing rapidly. He said Sunly is also actively negotiating with potential partners.

"The need for new data centres among major technology companies is large. A few years ago, Scandinavia and Finland were not preferred destinations for data centres. Since Western and Central European electricity grids have no short‑term capacity left for new data centres, attention has shifted to Scandinavia and Finland. Now those grids are also filling up, and data centres are looking for new locations," Aus explained.

According to Rungi, the moment when Greenergy can announce the addition of a major client may come very soon, but it may also take time.

"Sometimes where there is smoke, there is no fire, but sometimes there is," he said, adding that more than one good piece of news is coming. "Our industry is such that first we lay the egg and then we cackle."

Nebius' origins are linked to Yandex

Nebius may raise questions due to its connection to the Russian technology company Yandex, as Nebius emerged after Yandex came under sanctions following Russia's full‑scale invasion of Ukraine.

In 2024, the company sold its Russian business units and adopted the name Nebius Group, headquartered in the Netherlands. Nebius CEO Arkady Volozh is one of Yandex's founders, but he has since renounced Russian citizenship.

Rungi said Nebius is being labelled with things that are not true and that it is likely the most thoroughly scrutinised organisation in the entire chain.

"Because they were once connected to Russia, their burden is so heavy that it is even harder to gain trust. Yet they have earned trust from Meta, Microsoft, the US government, Nvidia and the New York Stock Exchange," he said. "I do not understand why this labelling continues."

Shared data hall equipment racks. Source: Tõnu Tunnel/Greenergy

Greenergy has operated for ten years, the first five spent on preparation, and has since offered services to the Estonian market while also investing in international expansion. A concern is Estonia's proximity to Russia, which causes hesitation among many potential foreign clients.

"At the same time, Finland has gained clients from this world and is also a neighbour of Russia (Nebius will build one of Europe's largest AI data centres in Finland by 2028). It is also about reputation, reliability, being known and trusted," Rungi said, adding that Greenergy has held hundreds of client meetings and practically all technology companies targeted by market players have visited them.

Aus said geopolitics is always part of negotiations with potential partners, but Estonia's membership in NATO and the European Union reduces risks for foreign partners.

Data centers could make a strong contribution to Estonia's GDP

If one major international client can be attracted to Estonia, finding additional clients will become much easier, Rungi said.

"This is a gravity business. If one comes, others follow. That is how it goes internationally; I have seen this pattern in many new markets. First come some crazy guys like us with an ambitious plan to do something that supposedly can never happen. Until the first breakthrough comes and the market develops," he said.

Aus agreed: once one major player establishes itself in the Baltics, validating the region as a data centre location, others will start looking more seriously, as has happened in Scandinavia and Finland.

"If we delay too long, until Western Europe's electricity grids catch up with demand, we will lose the opportunity to attract data centres here," Aus said.

Success, however, is hard‑won. Rungi said other countries offer tax incentives for such businesses, but Estonia does not, and there is no support from the export promotion system. He said established players are supported, but new ones do not qualify even when their ambitions are large and they have invested significant capital.

Data centres could bring substantial benefits to the state as a new economic sector. Rungi said that if Estonia's full potential were used, consuming local electricity and adding value through expertise, it would mean billions of euros annually in additional revenue for electricity companies and rental income for data centres, contributing a significant share to Estonia's GDP. The prerequisite is public acceptance.

Rungi said AI tends to be demonised, and although there are contexts where criticism is justified, accusations that data centres are to blame for energy consumption are unfair. He stressed that they do not consume energy for nothing – demand arises when people pay with a bank card or watch a film on Netflix.

"Just as a landfill is not to blame for the creation of waste, but people are, the same applies in the digital information space," he said. "We have a long way to go to make this clear."

He added that high water consumption in data centres is true in hot climates, but at Estonia's latitude, cooling is needed only for a small number of hours per year, which is a competitive advantage.

"The climate allows for much more efficient business, and in the end that means money," Rungi said.

Aus noted that Estonia currently has practically no energy‑intensive industry. For example, electricity consumption per capita in Norway is nearly four times higher than in Estonia, and in Sweden and Finland it is twice as high.

World.title: Chevron CFO bullish on Iraq after West Qurna 2, Nassiriya agreements
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Chevron boasts “significant potential” to expand its activities in Iraq over the next decade, according to Chief Financial Officer Eimear Bonner, highlighting the US oil company’s increasing trust in the country’s energy sector after recent deals with Baghdad.

Speaking to Bloomberg, Bonner said that Iraq remained one of Chevron’s top priority markets for future production expansion after the signing of preliminary agreements to pursue negotiations on the massive West Qurna 2 and Nassiriya oil fields.

She added that Chevron has been encouraged by its interaction with Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi and Iraq’s Ministry of Oil while discussions continue and that the corporation is also collaborating with Baghdad on diverse crude export routes to boost Iraq’s long-term energy security.

The statements bolster rising trust among foreign energy corporations after Al-Zaidi’s visit to the United States earlier this month, during which Iraq inked more than $60 billion in investment deals covering energy, infrastructure, banking, and technology.

World.title: Syria joins Saudi Arabia, Jordan in warning Iraq over Iran-backed militias
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Syria has joined Saudi Arabia and Jordan in warning Baghdad that strikes conducted from Iraqi soil against neighboring nations may result in military strikes against the armed groups responsible, according to Syrian military officials cited by regional media.

According to Al Jazeera and the US-funded Al Hurra, a senior Syrian military source said that Damascus will react to any strikes from Iraq by attacking the “terrorist militias” involved inside Iraqi territory.

The purported warning comes amid a steep increase in regional tensions after US-Saudi bombings against Iran-backed militias in Iraq in retaliation for drone assaults on Saudi oil installations, which Riyadh said were conducted from Iraqi territory.

The Iraqi government has frequently said that it would not allow Iraqi land to be used as a launchpad for attacks on neighboring nations.

Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi recently issued an order establishing a comprehensive security strategy aimed at enhancing state authority and preventing armed organizations from endangering regional security.

The new threat puts further pressure on Baghdad, as more neighboring nations indicate they may take direct action if cross-border assaults continue.

Iraqi authorities have attempted to prevent such a situation, claiming that security activities should be overseen by the Iraqi government rather than foreign forces.

Several Iran-backed organizations operating inside Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) are at the heart of the conflict, including Kataib Hezbollah, Asaib Ahl al-Haq, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada.

While the PMF is technically part of Iraq’s security system, some of its sections have strong links to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and have been accused by regional governments of carrying out strikes outside of Baghdad’s jurisdiction.

For Iraq, the diplomatic stakes go beyond security.

Baghdad has been attempting to reestablish ties with Syria as part of greater regional economic integration, including talks on resurrecting the old Iraq-Syria oil pipeline to the Mediterranean, which is considered strategically crucial for diversifying Iraq’s export routes outside the Gulf.

The purported Syrian warning comes at a critical moment for Al-Zaidi’s administration, which has spent recent months bolstering relations with Washington, Ankara, Riyadh, and Damascus while portraying Iraq as a secure destination for global investment.

The mounting threats from neighboring Arab governments highlight the importance of Baghdad demonstrating its ability to prevent armed groups from conducting strikes independent of the state.

Failure to do so risks increasing regional military tensions and jeopardizing Iraq’s aspirations to boost commerce, energy cooperation, and infrastructure projects with its neighbors.

The Syrian government has not issued an official warning, and IraqiNews.com has not independently confirmed the statements ascribed to the Syrian military source.

However, the claims reflect rising regional worry that strikes by Iran-backed militias operating from Iraqi soil could further destabilize the area and hamper Iraq’s diplomatic and economic goals.

World.title: Iran-backed militias threaten Iraq’s ties with US and Gulf
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Escalating tensions between Iran-backed militias are providing one of the most serious hurdles yet to Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s ambitions to deepen ties with the United States and Gulf states while luring billions of dollars in international investment.

The most recent crisis followed US-Saudi airstrikes on Iran-aligned armed groups in Iraq, when Saudi Arabia accused militias operating from Iraqi territory of firing drones at oil installations in the kingdom’s Eastern Province.

Riyadh claimed that the operation targeted the militias responsible for the assaults rather than the Iraqi state or its military forces, but Baghdad denounced the strikes as a breach of national sovereignty.

The recent tensions are being fueled by numerous prominent Iran-aligned organizations operating inside Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), notably Kataib Hezbollah, Asaib Ahl al-Haq, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada.

While the PMF is technically part of Iraq’s security apparatus, many of its groups have strong links to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and have occasionally conducted operations outside of Baghdad’s chain of command.

Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi responded by calling an emergency meeting of the Ministerial Council for National Security, canceling a planned trip to Saudi Arabia, and announcing a comprehensive security strategy to prevent Iraqi territory from being used to launch attacks on neighboring countries.

The administration also reiterated its resolve to keep all weapons entirely under state control.

That vow has gained importance after Al-Zaidi’s visit to Washington earlier this month, during which Iraq and the United States reiterated their commitment to completing the US-led coalition operation by the end of September 2026.

During the visit, Al-Zaidi pledged to ensure that all weapons eventually come into the control of the Iraqi state, citing it as a cornerstone of his government’s security strategy and a crucial step toward bolstering Iraq’s sovereignty and stability.

Since entering office, Al-Zaidi has maintained a policy of balancing Iraq’s ties with rival regional and international forces.

During recent travels to Washington, Ankara, and Tehran, he achieved huge investment and cooperation deals totaling tens of billions of dollars in the energy, banking, technology, infrastructure, and industrial sectors.

His administration has also attempted to strengthen connections with Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Turkey, and other Gulf nations via new transportation corridors, energy alliances, and trade agreements aimed at diversifying Iraq’s economy beyond oil and positioning the country as a regional center linking the Gulf to Europe.

According to analysts, Baghdad’s approach is highly dependent on proving that the Iraqi state, rather than armed groups, controls the country’s security and foreign policy.

Continued strikes from Iraqi territory risk eroding the country’s reputation with major regional allies and international investors, at a time when foreign investment has risen after years of turmoil.

The stakes rose when US President Donald Trump said that recent US-Saudi operations against Iran-backed militias were coordinated with the Iraqi government, a claim Baghdad has denied.

Observers believe it reflects rising discontent among Iraq’s leadership with armed groups accused of dragging the nation into regional conflicts that contradict Baghdad’s diplomatic and economic interests.

Al-Zaidi is currently facing the most significant test of his leadership.

Delivering on his promise to place all weapons under state control will be critical not only for Iraq’s internal security but also for maintaining trust with the United States, Gulf Arab states, and international investors, many of whom support many of the country’s largest economic projects.

Baghdad’s dilemma now extends beyond managing ties between Washington and Tehran.

It demonstrates that the Iraqi state possesses both the authority and the political will to prevent Iran-backed militias from using Iraqi territory to launch attacks that risk isolating the country, harming relations with Arab neighbors and the United States, and jeopardizing Iraq’s long-term economic recovery and investment goals.

World.title: Iraq faces growing fiscal strain
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is under increasing financial strain as plummeting oil earnings tighten government budgets, with Health Minister Abdul Hussein al-Mousawi saying that ensuring monthly public-sector wages has become the government’s top priority.

Speaking at a public meeting, al-Mousawi stated that the government requires approximately 10.8 trillion Iraqi dinars ($8.2 billion) per month to pay public-sector salaries, while current monthly oil revenues have fallen to approximately 2.5 trillion dinars, highlighting the growing gap between government obligations and income.

The statements are one of the most direct public acknowledgements by a top Iraqi official of the government’s financial challenges after months of decreased oil prices and fewer export profits.

Iraq’s government finances remain very vulnerable to variations in global energy markets because the vast bulk of public revenue comes from crude oil.

Official figures published this week indicated that oil accounted for over 84% of federal income in the first five months of 2026, but collections decreased by more than one-third compared to the same time the previous year as oil prices and export profits plummeted.

The health minister also warned of financing restrictions in the healthcare sector, citing worries about the supply of medications and the government’s capacity to sustain public services if financial pressures continue.

The fresh warnings follow weeks of increased regional tensions, which disrupted oil markets and added uncertainty to Iraq’s economic prospects.

As OPEC’s second-largest producer, Iraq relies on oil exports to fund wages, pensions, social welfare, and the majority of government expenditure, making the budget susceptible to long-term reductions in crude prices.

Economists have long cautioned that Iraq’s reliance on oil income makes the nation susceptible to external shocks, while a hefty public-sector pay bill constrains the government’s budgetary flexibility.

Previous administrations attempted to diversify income streams via tax changes and non-oil investments, but hydrocarbons remain the economy’s backbone.

The financial pressure comes at a critical time for Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s government, which has been promoting Iraq as a destination for billions of dollars in foreign investment following agreements signed with US, Turkish, and international companies in energy, banking, technology, and infrastructure.

Continued budgetary strain may make it more urgent to accelerate economic reforms, raise non-oil income, and improve public financial management to lessen Iraq’s reliance on petroleum exports.

They also emphasize that preserving investor trust will be contingent on the government’s ability to maintain macroeconomic stability while continuing to fund big development projects.

Despite the present issues, Iraq has large foreign currency reserves, which act as a financial cushion for the government.

However, experts warn that while reserves might help absorb short-term shocks, they are not a substitute for the fundamental changes needed to diversify the economy and reduce its dependence on unpredictable oil earnings.

World.title: Iraq expects record 22 million pilgrims for Arbaeen
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is prepared to welcome around 22 million pilgrims for this year’s Arbaeen pilgrimage, including up to 5 million overseas tourists, in what officials believe to be one of the country’s greatest religious gatherings and a significant boost to tourism and the local economy.

According to Iraqi official data, well over 22 million people are anticipated to attend the annual pilgrimage to the holy city of Karbala, with 4.5 million to 5 million pilgrims coming from outside Iraq.

The government has announced that tens of thousands of volunteers would be deployed to assist pilgrims, and Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has urged officials to boost the number of buses and other transport services to facilitate travel during the festival.

The surge of foreign tourists is projected to have a substantial impact on Iraq’s tourism, hospitality, transportation, and retail industries, with hotels, restaurants, transit operators, and local businesses benefitting from increased demand during the pilgrimage season.

Officials have extended transportation networks in preparation for this year’s pilgrimage, including more rail services, buses, and logistical assistance, as part of larger measures to boost connectivity and promote Iraq’s tourist industry.

The government has increasingly highlighted religious tourism as a crucial pillar of economic diversification, with millions of people visiting the country’s holy sites at Karbala, Najaf, Kadhimiya, and Samarra each year.

According to officials, continuing investment in infrastructure and tourist services will help Iraq become one of the Middle East’s major religious tourism destinations, while also creating jobs and helping local economies around the country.

World.title: Reports: Iraq PM threatened to resign over militia disarmament
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi has threatened to resign if Iran-aligned armed groups do not cooperate with his government’s efforts to bring all weapons under state control, according to reports citing political sources, highlighting the growing pressure on Baghdad to address one of its most difficult security challenges.

According to sources, Al-Zaidi warned leaders of Iraq’s Shi’ite Coordination Framework that if armed groups did not react to government efforts to disarm and completely submit to state authority, he would stand down.

IraqiNews.com was unable to independently verify the claims, and the Prime Minister’s office had no immediate response.

According to the sources, Al-Zaidi has been more dissatisfied by what he sees as a lack of cooperation on one of his administration’s fundamental commitments: guaranteeing that all weapons stay solely under the control of the Iraqi government.

The claims came days after US-Saudi airstrikes struck Iran-backed groups in Iraq in response to drone assaults on Saudi oil installations, which Riyadh said were launched from Iraqi territory.

The bombings forced Al-Zaidi to call an emergency security conference, cancel a planned trip to Saudi Arabia, and unveil a new security strategy aimed at preventing Iraqi territory from being used to launch attacks on neighboring nations.

Armed organizations have emerged as one of Al-Zaidi’s most pressing problems.

Since entering office, he has attempted to solicit billions of dollars in foreign investment with trips to Washington, Tehran, and Ankara, while portraying Iraq as a stable location for oil, infrastructure, and technological projects.

Analysts believe Baghdad’s economic objectives are strongly dependent on its ability to show that the state, not armed groups, controls Iraq’s security strategy.

Repeated strikes conducted from Iraqi territory have strained ties with regional allies and risk weakening investor trust.

According to Western diplomatic sources published by Asharq Al-Awsat, key Iraqi officials, including Al-Zaidi and members of Iraq’s security apparatus, have received threats in connection with the government’s attempts to restrict weaponry outside of state control.

Unlike many regional leaders, Iraq’s prime minister leads by wide political agreement rather than a legislative majority, restricting his power to make unilateral choices.

Major security and political changes usually need agreement among Iraq’s different political blocs.

Al-Zaidi’s biggest power may not be the threat of resignation, but rather the international backing his administration has garnered as a result of recent accords with the United States, Turkey, and other allies.

These agreements, which span energy, finance, technology, and infrastructure, have boosted hopes that Iraq will attract tens of billions of dollars in investment if security improves.

Whether Al-Zaidi can translate that international momentum into domestic reforms will ultimately depend on gaining broader political support for his pledge to keep all weapons under Iraqi state control, which has become one of his government’s most closely watched tests.

World.title: Iraq denies launching strikes from its territory against neighboring nations
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The military spokesperson for the Iraqi commander-in-chief, Sabah al-Numan, confirmed on Thursday that neither a foreign nor local body has presented proof that recent regional drone attacks were launched from Iraqi territory.

In a statement to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), al-Numan urged accusing parties to submit reliable proof, saying that Baghdad has yet to receive such data.

The development comes following statements made by the Saudi Ministry of Defense, alleging that drone attacks targeting key oil infrastructure in the past few days originated in Iraq.

The Iraqi official indicated that the government will neither tolerate unilateral military acts from within its borders nor accept foreign violations of its territorial sovereignty.

Al-Numan’s remarks come a day after the United States and Saudi Arabia launched coordinated airstrikes targeting several bases of Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), killing and injuring many fighters.

The joint operation targeted several logistical and weapons storage locations in different provinces in Iraq, escalating the current regional battle.

The PMF described the joint US-Saudi strike as a dangerous escalation and a clear breach of Iraqi sovereignty.

World.title: Iraqi oil flows to continue via Turkey’s Ceyhan as renewal deal is discussed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Turkish sources told Reuters that crude oil shipments from northern Iraq to the Turkish port of Ceyhan will continue while the two countries seek an arrangement to extend the pipeline’s operation for another 12 months.

On July 27, a bilateral agreement that had been in place for decades ended. Despite expectations, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi did not sign a 12-month renewal deal during his meeting with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Ankara on Tuesday.

According to a Turkish official, oil flows via the Iraq-Turkey pipeline, which is Baghdad’s only operational export pipeline, will continue while negotiations for a renewal deal are still in progress.

Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar recently announced a 12-month extension agreement between the two countries.

During a joint press conference in Ankara, Erdogan stated on Tuesday that Turkey hopes to finalize a comprehensive energy cooperation agreement as soon as possible.

An extension is intended to provide additional time for discussions on a complete accord. Turkey aims to fully utilize the 1.5 million barrels per day pipeline and consider expanding it to oil fields in southern Iraq.

Turkish data suggests that the pipeline currently transports approximately 170,000 barrels per day.

World.title: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke falls sick again while meeting people in building parking
World.content:
Dipke's father, Bhagwan Dipke, said doctors had been called to examine his son.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke fell ill again on Saturday morning after feeling uneasy and vomiting while meeting supporters at his residence in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, days after revealing that he had been diagnosed with typhoid.The incident occurred at around 11.45 am, when Dipke came down to the parking area of his residence to meet a group of people waiting to see him.According to those present, he suddenly felt unwell and moved to the rear of the building, where he vomited. He later returned upstairs to his residence without speaking to the media.Confirming the incident, Dipke's father, Bhagwan Dipke, said doctors had been called to examine his son.Dipke had disclosed on July 25, during the protests at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, that he had been diagnosed with typhoid. At the time, he said he had been unwell for several days and was undergoing treatment.

World.title: PM Modi inaugurates Rs 5,000 crore Bhogapuram Airport in Andhra Pradesh
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Saturday inaugurated the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram in

's Vizianagaram district, a nearly Rs 5,000 crore project that the state government says will transform North Andhra into a major economic and industrial hub.

The PM was accorded a grand ceremonial welcome, with around 13,500 tribal women performing the traditional Dhimsa dance. The airport premises were adorned with displays celebrating Andhra Pradesh's rich cultural heritage, including Etikoppaka artwork and motifs depicting the state's geographical identity.

PM Modi was received by Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu, deputy chief minister Pawan Kalyan, and union civil aviation minister K Ram Mohan Naidu.

He later witnessed the Dhimsa performance before formally inaugurating the airport.

Developed by the GMR Group, the airport has been named after freedom fighter Alluri Sitarama Raju. It has been designed to handle six million passengers annually in its first phase, with a long-term expansion plan to increase capacity to 40 million passengers a year. Commercial flight operations are scheduled to begin on August 17.

World.title: 'Enjoys playing victim card': Congress attacks PM Modi's 'forgive youth' remark
World.content:
Jairam Ramesh accuses PM Modi of playing 'victim card'

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Saturday criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his remarks about "forgiving" the country's youth.He said the Prime Minister should instead apologise over a range of issues, including alleged exam paper leaks, the treatment of student protesters, demonetisation and the functioning of the Ram Mandir Trust.In a post on X, Ramesh said, "The self-declared non-biological PM enjoys playing the victim card." He further alleged that the Prime Minister "uses vile vitriol against his predecessors and political opponents" and "very frequently peddles lies to defame them, not just in his public speeches but in Parliament itself.""He uses vile vitriol against his predecessors and political opponents. He very frequently peddles lies to defame them, not just in his public speeches but in Parliament itself. He unleashes an army of foul-mouthed abusers both in Parliament and outside and gives them full protection," Ramesh said.Referring to the National Testing Agency (NTA) and student protests, Ramesh said, "the entire nation is wanting the PM to apologise for the trauma inflicted on lakhs of youth through his paper leak-ridden NTA and his Home Ministry-sanctioned brutality on student protestors."He also said the Prime Minister owed an apology over the "Chanda Chori Astha Dhoka by the Ram Mandir Trust" and for the "Tughlakian notebandi of Nov 8 2016 that destroyed crores of livelihoods and shuttered lakhs if MSMEs."Ramesh added, "but late last night, in act of supreme self-obsession, the PM said that he forgave our youth." He alleged that the remark was "an insult to the nation and to our youth", adding that young people had suffered under the government's policies and were instead seeking an apology from the Prime Minister."The Prime Ministerâs InstaGram Sabhas are fooling no one," Ramesh added.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday shared a video late at night that carried a message against abusive language and hate, saying "abuses never solve anything," amid a controversy over alleged derogatory remarks made against him by a woman from Noida during a protest in Delhi."Abuses never solve anything. Letâs guide the misguided. Letâs work together. Letâs work for Bharat," PM Modi wrote, sharing the video on X.In the video, PM Modi also highlighted the government's efforts to strengthen the country's examination system, citing Parliament's passage of a stringent anti-paper leak law."Friends, we are continuously taking one step after another to build a trustworthy examination system. Whether it is creating fast-track mechanisms or incorporating suggestions from the states, we are working in that direction."The Prime Minister said paper leaks had affected governments across the country for decades and jeopardised the future of students.PM Modi reiterated that the government would act firmly against those involved in paper leak rackets.

World.title: FSSAI cracks down on three firms over food safety violations
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has launched a fresh enforcement drive against food business operators, issuing a product recall, suspending a manufacturing licence and prohibiting the sale of a health supplement over serious violations of food safety regulations.

In one action, FSSAI ordered M/s Sun Organic Industries Pvt Ltd to immediately recall its Wonderland Raisins after regulatory testing found pesticide residues exceeding the prescribed limits. Samples tested at both the National Food Laboratory, Ghaziabad, and the Referral Laboratory, NIFTEM-K, were declared "unsafe" under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The company has been directed to recall the entire batch from the market and submit periodic recall status reports.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

In a separate action, the food regulator suspended the licence of Dior Pharmaceuticals' Nutraceutical Manufacturing Unit with immediate effect after an inspection revealed major and critical non-compliances. According to FSSAI, the unit failed to comply with several regulatory and hygiene requirements, including inadequate quality management systems and deficiencies in manufacturing practices.

FSSAI also issued a prohibition order against M/s Vatave Health Care, banning the manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of its Folineuro Syrup (Folinic Acid Syrup). The regulator said the product was marketed as a nutritional food supplement with misleading claims related to brain function despite not complying with provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act and the Food Safety and Standards (Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals, Food for Special Dietary Use, Food for Special Medical Purpose, Functional Food and Novel Food) Regulations, 2016.

The regulator said the actions were taken to protect consumers and ensure compliance with food safety laws. It warned that violations of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, would invite strict legal and penal action.

World.title: 'Same people who litter here, use dustbin abroad': Bombay HC on civic sense
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court on Friday came down heavily on Indians who litter public places at home but follow cleanliness rules abroad, saying the same people who "throw garbage on the road without batting an eyelid" in India ensure to put "even a small chocolate wrapper" in the dustbin abroad.

The court stressed that maintaining cleanliness is a fundamental duty and called for strict action against offenders.

A bench of Justices G S Kulkarni and Aarti Sathe made the observations while hearing a batch of petitions over pollution, foul odour, gas emissions and health hazards linked to the Kanjurmarg dumping ground in Mumbai.

The judges said public participation was essential to keeping the city clean and urged civic authorities to enforce the rules without hesitation.

"If a person wants a clean environment, then he or she has a corresponding fundamental duty towards society to maintain cleanliness. We want the civic officials to be ruthless in taking action," the court said according to news agency PTI.

Expressing concern over people's attitude towards public cleanliness, the bench said citizens often behave differently once they leave India.

"We have to sensitise our citizens. Here, a person will throw garbage on the road without batting an eyelid, but these same people, when abroad, will strictly avoid such behaviour.





Even a small chocolate wrapper they will throw in the dustbin," the high court said.

The bench then questioned, "Is this the price of liberty and democracy?"

The court also voiced concern over the large quantity of plastic waste strewn across public places, observing that even Mumbai's beaches are littered with plastic. It questioned whether such conditions reflected the standards of "a civilised society".

The judges noted that garbage dumped on roads and in narrow lanes poses serious health and hygiene risks to residents every day.

Referring to the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai's slogan 'Swachch Mumbai, Sundar Mumbai, Aapli Mumbai, Sundar Mumbai', the court said the civic body's intention was commendable but was being undermined by irresponsible behaviour from citizens and inadequate enforcement by the municipal machinery.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"It is in these circumstances the role of MCGM's cleanliness machinery wardwise becomes significant, to take all effective steps so that public streets are not used by the citizens as dumping places," the bench observed.

The court said failing to enforce the rules would defeat the objective behind the civic body's cleanliness campaign and urged authorities to implement the existing regulations strictly.

It also raised concerns over the handling of garbage near heritage landmarks such as Rajabai Tower and the Bombay high court building. The bench observed that tourists, including foreign visitors, often encounter garbage on roads because of poor waste handling by municipal collection vehicles.

The high court directed the civic body to take corrective steps within a week, warning that it would otherwise be compelled to pass further orders.

World.title: First J&K terror attack on migrants in 21 months: Two Chhattisgarh labourers die after being shot
World.content:
The attack took place late Friday night in the Kelam area of south Kashmir (File photo)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The death toll in Friday night's terror attack on migrant labourers in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam rose to two on Saturday after a Chhattisgarh worker succumbed to injuries in hospital, officials told news agency PTI.The attack took place late Friday night in the Kelam area of south Kashmir, where the two workers were employed at a brick kiln. Officials said both men sustained critical injuries after terrorists fired at them.One of the labourers, identified as Deepak Ratray, died before he could be shifted to a hospital. The second victim, Bopinder, was initially admitted to Government Medical College (GMC) Anantnag before being referred to SKIMS Hospital in Soura, where he later succumbed to his injuries.Officials said both victims were in their twenties and had travelled from Chhattisgarh in search of work.The incident comes days after terrorists shot dead Jammu and Kashmir Police head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi at Anantnag's Lal Chowk while he was deployed on Amarnath Yatra duty. That attack, on July 22, was the first terror strike in Kashmir since the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam massacre, in which 26 people were killed.Friday's attack has also revived concerns over the safety of migrant workers in the Valley. In February 2024, two non-local labourers from Punjab, Amritpal Singh and Rohit Masih, were shot dead in Srinagar. Before that, in October 2021, terrorists killed two workers from Bihar, Raja Reshi Dev and Joginder Reshi Dev, in Kulgam's Wanpoh area.Lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha condemned the latest attack and said security forces had been instructed to intensify anti-terror operations."I strongly condemn this cowardly act. I have directed our security forces to step up their operations and eliminate the terrorists," Sinha wrote on X, adding that he had spoken to DGP Nalin Prabhat and other senior security officials.PDP president and former chief minister Mehbooba Mufti also condemned the killings."They work themselves to the bone far away from home only to feed their families. Unimaginably cruel to target them in such senseless acts of violence," she said.BJP's Jammu and Kashmir spokesperson Altaf Thakur described the attack as "cowardly, barbaric and inhuman", alleging that its objective was to disturb peace and normalcy in the Union Territory.The attack occurred during the ongoing Amarnath Yatra, which began on July 3. While the pilgrimage through the Pahalgam route has remained suspended since July 19 because of heavy rain and landslides, the Baltal route in Ganderbal continues to remain operational.Following the attack, security forces launched a cordon-and-search operation in the area to trace those responsible.

World.title: India screens nearly 11,000 travellers after Ebola emergency, no case detected
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India has screened 10,974 international travellers arriving from Ebola-affected countries since May 23 after the World Health Organization declared the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC), with no case detected in the country so far, the Centre informed Parliament on Friday.

The government said surveillance and preparedness were intensified across the country following the WHO declaration, with enhanced screening at airports and other points of entry, mandatory travel declarations, designated isolation facilities, expanded laboratory capacity and nationwide mock drills to prepare for any suspected case.

According to the ministry of health and family welfare, all international passengers are screened for recent travel to Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda and South Sudanâcountries affected by the Ebola outbreak.

The government has not imposed a blanket travel ban, but passengers with travel history to these countries during the previous 21 days are identified through Self Declaration Forms, including the Air Suvidha 2.0 portal.

Mumbai accounted for the highest number of screened passengers at 7,568, followed by Delhi (1,833), Hyderabad (532), Chennai (210), Bengaluru (205) and Ahmedabad (200). At the state level, Gujarat recorded the highest number of screened passengers (2,905), followed by Maharashtra (2,228), Uttar Pradesh (785), Tamil Nadu (731), Telangana (624) and Kerala (554).





Replying to a question in the Lok Sabha, Union Health Minister J P Nadda said the Centre had coordinated its response with the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Civil Aviation and other agencies to strengthen surveillance and preparedness.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The preparedness measures include issuing standard operating procedures covering surveillance, quarantine, laboratory testing, infection prevention and clinical management; identifying and operationalising isolation facilities across states and Union Territories; expanding diagnostic capacity through ICMR-NIV Pune and additional Biosafety Level-3 laboratories; deploying additional doctors and paramedical staff at major international airports; and conducting mock drills in designated hospitals nationwide.

The government has also strengthened public awareness through airport displays, in-flight announcements, social media campaigns and a 24Ã7 national helpline while activating the NCDC Public Health Emergency Operations Centre to coordinate the response.

The health ministry said no Ebola case has been reported in India so far.

World.title: Suspected Ebola case in Delhi: BSF constable from Congo mission admitted to RML, sample sent for testing
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A 52-year-old BSF constable who recently returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo as part of an Indian UN peacekeeping contingent has been admitted to the isolation ward at the Ebola Nursing Home of Dr Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital after developing fever during mandatory quarantine, triggering Ebola surveillance protocols.

The constable, who arrived in India on July 11, had been under a 21-day quarantine at the Airport Health Organisation (APHO) facility following his return from Congo, an Ebola-endemic region. On the evening of 20th day of quarantine, he developed a fever along with body aches.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

As per protocol, he was shifted to the designated Ebola isolation facility at RML Hospital. His blood sample has been sent to the National Institute of Virology (NIV), Pune, for confirmatory testing.

The test report is awaited.

Officials said the patient is being managed in strict isolation while health authorities continue to monitor the situation. At present, the case remains suspected, and Ebola infection has not been confirmed.

India follows enhanced screening and quarantine measures for personnel returning from Ebola-affected regions. Suspected cases are isolated immediately and samples are tested at designated reference laboratories before a diagnosis is confirmed.

World.title: PM Modi inaugurates Bhogapuram international airport, launches projects worth ₹17,900 crore in A.P. | Live
World.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram in Vizianagaram district on Saturday (August 1, 2026), giving Andhra Pradesh its first greenfield international airport since the 2014 bifurcation.

Built at a cost of over ₹5,640 crore by GMR Visakhapatnam International Airport Limited under a public-private partnership, the airport is designed to handle six million passengers a year in its first phase. Mr. Modi cut the ribbon at the terminal, and will inspect the facilities and address a public meeting. He was received by Governor S. Abdul Nazeer and Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu.

He also laid foundation stones for projects worth more than ₹17,900 crore across the State. including a semiconductor plant at Visakhapatnam, transmission works for renewable energy zones in Kurnool and Anantapur, and four national highway projects.Scheduled commercial flights at Bhogapuram will begin on August 17, when civil operations cease at the Visakhapatnam airport.

The visit is also Mr. Modi’s first public programme since the protests at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi.

World.title: PM playing ‘victim card’ instead of apologising for brutality on protesting students: Congress
World.content:
The Congress on Saturday (August 1, 2026) said that Narendra Modi is playing the victim card by saying he has forgiven the youth who abused him, and demanded an apology from the Prime Minister for the “brutality” unleashed on student protestors and the trauma they suffered due to paper leaks.

The Opposition party also claimed that the Prime Minister's "InstaGram sabhas”, which it termed an act of “supreme self-obsession”, are fooling no one.

“Late last night, in an act of supreme self-obsession, the Prime Minister said that he forgave our youth. This is an insult to the nation and to our youth, which has suffered under his government and is legitimately demanding an apology from him. The Prime Minister's InstaGram Sabhas are fooling no one,” Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said in a post on X.

In an Instagram video posted on Friday (July 31, 2026) night, Mr. Modi said it pained him that even his late mother was subjected to “filthy abuses” at the Jantar Mantar and lamented that “our daughters” had used such language, even as he called for forgiving the “misguided children”.

The Prime Minister said he could understand the anguish prevailing in society, but stressed that this was the time to embrace the youth and guide them on the right path.

In his post, Mr. Ramesh said, “The self-declared non-biological PM enjoys playing the victim card.” The Congress leader also said that Mr. Modi uses “vile vitriol” against his predecessors and political opponents.

“He very frequently peddles lies to defame them, not just in his public speeches but in Parliament itself. He unleashes an army of foul-mouthed abusers both in Parliament and outside and gives them full protection.The entire nation is wanting the PM to apologise for the trauma inflicted on lakhs of youth through his paper leak-ridden NTA and his Home Ministry-sanctioned brutality on student protestors.

“The entire nation is waiting for the PM to apologise for the 'Chanda Chori Astha Dhoka' by the Ram Mandir Trust, an establishment which he had grandly announced in the Lok Sabha on February 5, 2020. The entire nation is still expecting his apology for his Tughlakian notebandi of November 8, 2016, that destroyed crores of livelihoods and shuttered lakhs of MSMEs. The list is endless,” the Congress leader said.

World.title: West Asia war LIVE: White House signals Trump is weighing new strikes on Iran
World.content:
The White House signalled that U.S. President Donald Trump is weighing carrying out new strikes on Iran as the U.S. presses for Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and abide by terms set out in a truce agreement the two sides forged last month, only to quickly collapse.

Also Read | Trump announces deal for ‘complete disarmament’ of Hamas

There were no U.S. strikes on Iran overnight, but Iran’s paramilitary Revolutionary Guard said on Friday (July 31, 2026) it had struck another two tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, and Kuwait said it intercepted drones.

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt expressed the U.S. administration’s frustration anew, charging that Tehran last month signed a memorandum of understanding with the US on a truce but then quickly “broke it, shot at commercial ships, and killed American soldiers”.

World.title: Kerala heavy rains LIVE: IMD issues red alert for 9 districts
World.content:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) upgraded the rain alert for Kerala by issuing a red alert for nine districts, warning of extreme heavy rainfall over the next 24 hours. The remaining five districts were placed on orange alert, where very heavy rainfall is likely on August 1, 2026.

Also read | At least one dead after landslip hits Idukki

Kasaragod, Kannur, Wayanad, Kozhikode, Malappuram, Thrissur, Idukki, Kottayam, and Pathanamthitta have been placed on red alert.

In the wake of heavy rains continuing in various parts of Kerala and reports of landslips and mudslides in some places, Chief Minister V.D. Satheeshan contacted the Revenue Minister, the Chief Secretary, and the District Collectors.

Disaster prevention activities will be coordinated by the Revenue Minister. The Revenue Minister has convened a meeting of District Collectors at 11 a.m. NDRF, police, and others are prepared to handle any situation, said the Chief Minister.

World.title: Kerala's Water Resources Department to draw up short and long-term development plans covering five years
World.content:
Kerala’s Water Resources Department is drawing up short and long-term action plans for improving its operational efficiency over the next five years.

With this aim in mind, the State government is planning to organise a conclave in Thiruvananthapuram in mid-August where schemes and proposals for the plans would be discussed. Broadly, the short-term action plan would be for a one-year period, while the long-term one would cover five years.

The aims include the introduction of timely changes in operational matters, overcoming limitations and flaws and the roll-out of technological innovations, according to the Water Resources Department.

Considered a water-abundant State, Kerala, nevertheless, faces unique challenges related to water supply and access, sanitation and groundwater contamination. “Wells continue to serve as a primary source of water for a significant portion of the population in Kerala. Concerns regarding water quality, particularly microbiological contamination, have emerged as critical issues requiring urgent attention,” the Kerala Development Report 2026 of the State Planning Board, published in March 2026, had noted. The report further observed that, “Groundwater contamination can be caused by poorly designed and maintained septic tanks, along with inadequate sewage and septage management, emphasising the need for improved sanitation infrastructure and groundwater protection to ensure safe drinking water.”

Under its Vision 2031 roadmap, the new Congress-ledd UDF government in Kerala has announced plans for special missions and a commission for tackling issues related to integrated water management and protection of wetlands and rivers. Proposals include a Kerala River Basin and Water Systems Mission, a Wetland Mission, and a Water Commission with the involvement of multiple departments. The Revised Budget for 2026-27, presented by the UDF government, has earmarked ₹895.59 crore for water supply and sanitation.

The Kerala Development Report had also emphasised the need to combine supply-side augmentation, integrated water management and demand-side efficiency with tech-innovative and participatory practices.

World.title: Delhi court expresses disappointment over NCB's conduct in contesting bail pleas
World.content:
A Delhi court has expressed disappointment over the conduct of the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) in contesting bail applications after its officials failed to specify evidence linking an accused to a case.

Also read | 255 drug offenders held in 48-hour crackdown

Hearing the bail plea of the accused, Special Judge Jitendra Pratap Singh directed the NCB zonal director to furnish an explanation on the agency's insufficient response in countering the plea.

In the order dated July 30, the court said that neither the original investigating officer nor the case handling officer had been able to specify the material that directly connects the applicant or accused to the alleged offence.

“With great reluctance, this court is expressing its disappointment as to the conduct of the affairs of the agency in contesting the bail applications.

“On account of heavy pendency of the matters before the court, generally a notice of about 45 days on bail applications is issued, and on several such occasions, the court has to adjourn the hearing for want of requisite assistance from the prosecution.

“In such circumstances, it is directed that the copy of this order be placed before the zonal director, NCB, asking him to furnish an explanation in light of the reply to the instant bail application,” Mr. Singh said.

He directed the NCB director to state whether the reply filed in the matter is sufficient for recording the agency's opposition to the present bail application.

World.title: ‘Another low’: Kapil Sibal slams saffron colour change of hockey jersey
World.content:
Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal on Saturday (August 1, 2026) slammed the change of jersey colour of the Indian hockey team from the traditional blue to saffron as "another low" that had not been seen before.

The Indian men's and women's hockey teams will be seen in saffron jerseys instead of their traditional blue kits at next month's FIH World Cup in the Netherlands and Belgium, a change that has been questioned by former players but defended as a technical necessity by Hockey India.

"FIH Hockey World Cup: Teams traditional: Blue Jersey Turns Saffron! Neither the Hockey India President nor the Executive Board knew," Sibal said on X.

"Logic: If the jersey is saffron, the mind may turn saffron! Another low, not seen before!" the Independent Rajya Sabha MP said.

Unveiling the new jersey on its social media pages, Hockey India said the design and colour of the jersey is meant to "tell a story" and carry "India's pride" and was finalised after consultations with players and support staff.

The body said saffron symbolises courage, sacrifice and victory and no external pressure guided its decision.

"It was observed that the blue playing uniform tended to blend/merge with the blue synthetic playing surface, which is now the standard colour of international hockey pitches. This visual similarity affected on-field clarity and visibility for the players," Hockey India said in a statement after former captains like Viren Rasquinha questioned the logic behind the move.

All the same, Hockey India President Dilip Tirkey said the decision was taken without his knowledge. Secretary Bhola Nath Singh differed, insisting that "all officials were aware" of the change.

The move has also invited scathing criticism from former players such as Vasudevan Bhaskaran, Viren Rasquinha, Ajit Pal Singh, and Pargat Singh, all of whom questioned the logic behind such a move that may affect the team's identity built over decades.

World.title: DMK chief Stalin asks T.N. CM Vijay to convene all-party meeting on Cauvery dispute
World.content:
DMK president and former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin on Saturday (August 1, 2026) asked Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay whether he would convene an all-party meeting to discuss the Cauvery water dispute.

Referring to recent developments in Karnataka, Mr. Stalin said the neighbouring State had demonstrated political unity on the issue.

“The Karnataka Chief Minister initially invited Mr. Vijay for talks but has now asked him not to visit and instead convened an all-party meeting on August 2. This shows that all political parties in Karnataka are united on the Cauvery issue,” he said in a social media post.

Recalling his earlier advice that talks with Karnataka would not help Tamil Nadu, Mr. Stalin said that was why he had urged the Chief Minister not to visit the neighbouring State.

“A legal battle is the only way to deal with a State that has consistently denied Tamil Nadu its rightful share of Cauvery water. Karnataka treats Tamil Nadu as a destination only for surplus water. But Mr. Vijay appears to have believed that he could secure water by holding talks,” he said.

Mr. Stalin said Karnataka had asked Mr. Vijay not to visit after the Cauvery Water Management Authority directed the State to release water to Tamil Nadu.

“We anticipated these developments and therefore urged the Chief Minister to convene an all-party meeting. Will he do so now?” Mr. Stalin asked.

World.title: Search operation to locate 7 climbers missing after Broad Peak avalanche resumes
World.content:
GILGIT: A search and rescue operation to locate seven climbers part of a 10-member team that went missing after an avalanche at Broad Peak earlier this week resumed on Saturday morning.

The operation was suspended late Friday due to adverse weather conditions in the region.

The bodies of three climbers — Oman’s Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy, Nepal’s Pur Bahadur Gurung and American Mallory Geis — were found on Friday and airlifted to Skardu.

The missing climbers include five from Nepal, including renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja, Kili Pemba Sherpa, Nima Sherpa, Nawang Thindu Sherpa and Gyalu Sherpa. Pakistan’s climber Sohail Sakhi and China’s Wang Zhong are also among those missing.

According to the local administration, a three-member civil rescue team, led by renowned mountaineer Sarbaz Khan, was taking part in the search and rescue operation.

The team started their ground mission again on Saturday morning to locate the seven missing climbers. Additionally, Nepali climbers present at the basecamp with other expedition teams were also taking part in the operation.

Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) President Major General Irfan Arshad told Dawn that the search operation was underway at Broad Peak. He said Pakistan Army helicopters were also heading towards the area where the climbers went missing.

The club’s general secretary, Ayaz Shigri, also told Dawn that the rescue operation was being carried out with support of army helicopters.

He said that during the operation the rescue teams had identified the presence of more climbers at an altitude of 6,000m through drone footage.

“Mountain terrain, adverse weather, snow avalanche risks and snowfall create difficulties for rescue team members,” he said.

According to Nepali media, renowned Nepali mountaineer Mingma David Sherpa arrived in Pakistan to assist the search and rescue operation. David travelled from Nepal to join the ongoing efforts to locate Purja and the other missing climbers.

The avalanche struck while the mountaineers were on a mission to summit Broad Peak (8,047 metres, 26,400 feet) on Thursday while the team was ascending at an altitude of around 6,600 metres, according to regional authorities.

The team was last in contact on Thursday morning, an official statement said, with reports emerging that evening of the powerful avalanche.

“Data from their tracking devices indicates that they were thrown hundreds of metres down the mountainside,” Naila Kiani, from Pakistan’s Alpine Club, told Le Monde newspaper.

Additional input from AFP

World.title: Religious scholar affiliated with JUI-F shot dead in Lower South Waziristan
World.content:
LOWER SOUTH WAZIRISTAN: A religious scholar affiliated with the Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F), Maulana Muhammad Ismail, was shot dead by unidentified armed men in the Azam Warsak area of Birmal tehsil in Lower South Waziristan, it emerged on Saturday.

District Police Officer (DPO) Muhammad Tahir said that the incident occurred after Friday prayers when unidentified assailants on a motorcycle opened fire on Ismail, killing him on the spot. The official said the assailants managed to escape from the scene.

The DPO said that an initial report of the incident had been registered and an investigation into the killing had been launched. He added that police were examining the incident from all angles.

According to police officials and local tribal elders, the deceased was a resident of Kazha Panga and was serving as a teacher at a religious seminary in the area.

In May, renowned cleric and former JUI-F MPA Maulana Muhammad Idrees was killed in Charsadda after unidentified assailants opened fire on him.

World.title: Modi says he forgives protesters who abused him during youth-led demonstrations against exam paper leaks
World.content:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said he wanted to “forgive” protesters who abused him during recent youth-led demonstrations that dealt a rare political setback to his government.

The remarks came after the online Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) mobilised large protests in New Delhi and other cities over examination paper leaks, posing the biggest challenge to Modi’s government in recent years.

Some protesters featured in widely circulated videos shouting insults at the prime minister have since faced online abuse from Modi supporters as well as police complaints, according to local media reports.

Police have also asked social media platforms, including Meta and X, to take down what they described as abusive and manipulated content targeting the premier.

“The country and the world witnessed what happened at Jantar Mantar. Some mischievous youngsters hurled vile abuses,” Modi, 75, said in a video posted on Instagram late on Friday.

“Words were used that do not belong to civilised society — directed not just at me, but even at my late mother … I want to forgive them.”

Modi also said “mistakes made in youth” should be corrected through guidance rather than legal action, referring to the police cases.

The protests that began last month were initially sparked by anger over examination paper leaks.

But they broadened into a wider expression of frustration over unemployment and governance, culminating in the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

Since the protests began, Modi has increasingly used Instagram — the platform on which the CJP built much of its support — to communicate directly with youngsters.

Modi’s ruling party has 9.6 million Instagram followers, while the CJP, launched only in May, has more than 26m.

World.title: Naqvi’s remarks ignite fresh debate in political circles
World.content:
ISLAMABAD / HYDERABAD / LAHORE: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s call for an overhaul of the country’s governance structure and the carving out of new administrative units has ignited an animated debate across the country, with the PPP referring the question to its top decision-making forum, the Sindh chief minister flatly rejecting it, Lahore’s lawyers terming it unconstitutional and Sindhi nationalist groups demanding the minister’s resignation.

Addressing the Pakistan Economic Summit in Islamabad on Thursday, Mr Naqvi said the present system of governance had collapsed and was fundamentally incapable of resolving the country’s problems.

He urged all political parties to sit together and settle every outstanding issue, including the creation of new units and provinces, warning that without structural change the same debates would be taking place a decade from now.

He described more administrative units as the only way to bring facilities closer to citizens, said new leadership was needed, and argued that the country’s youth wanted justice, merit and jobs rather than stipends and laptops.

PPP refers matter to CEC

The PPP’s Central Executive Com­mittee will take up the question of new administrative units, party secretary general Nayyar Bokhari told Dawn, while insisting that the route must be constitutional rather than executive.

Bokhari said the Constitution laid down a complete procedure, and that neither new provinces nor any change in provincial boundaries was possible without a two-thirds majority in the relevant provincial assembly, the National Assembly and the Senate. New provinces, he stressed, could not be brought about through an executive order. He said that if there was genuine seriousness about creating new provinces — South Punjab included — the matter should go to parliament and the constitutional requirements should be met.

Mr Bokhari called on Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, whose party governs Punjab and the Centre, to begin the process in his own province, recalling that a resolution for a South Punjab province was already pending before the Punjab Assembly.
